sentences.zh: 西喇布子馬喇希阿蘭珠阿蘭珠弟布爾堪納爾察納爾察子瑚沙

translations.literal: Xilabu and his son Malaxi; Alanzhu; Alanzhu's younger brother Bu'erkan; Na'ercha; Na'ercha's son Husha.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies in this volume include Xilabu and his son Malaxi, Alanzhu, Alanzhu's younger brother Bu'erkan, Na'ercha, and Na'ercha's son Husha.

sentences.zh: 達音布朗格朗格子和託從弟雍舜瑪爾當圖瑪爾當圖子烏庫理

translations.literal: Dayin; Bulangge; Langge and his son Hetuo; Hetuo's younger cousin Yongshun; Ma'erdangtu; Ma'erdangtu's son Wukuli.
translations.idiomatic: Also treated here are Dayin, Bulangge, Langge and his son Hetuo, Hetuo's younger cousin Yongshun, Ma'erdangtu, and Ma'erdangtu's son Wukuli.

sentences.zh: 喀喇喀喇孫舒裡渾洛多歡崆古圖巴篤理穆克譚穆克譚子愛音塔穆達珠瑚}}=揚古利=揚古利，舒穆祿氏，世居渾春。

translations.literal: Kala; Kala's grandson Shuli; Hun; Luoduo; Kuangutu; Baduli; Muketan; Muketan's son Aiyin; Tamuda; Zhuhu. Yangguli, of the Shumulu clan, had long resided at Hunchun.
translations.idiomatic: This volume also covers Kala, his grandson Shuli, Hun, Luoduo, Kuangutu, Baduli, Muketan and his son Aiyin, Tamuda, Zhuhu, and Yangguli. Yangguli belonged to the Shumulu clan and came from a family long settled at Hunchun.

sentences.zh: 父郎柱，爲庫爾喀部長，率先附太祖，時通往來，太祖遇之厚，命揚古利入侍。

translations.literal: His father Langzhu was chief of the Kurka tribe and was the first to submit to Taizu. Because communications were then open, Taizu treated him generously and ordered Yangguli to enter attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His father Langzhu was chief of the Kurka tribe and was the first to submit to Nurhaci. With regular contact established, the khan treated him generously and had Yangguli enter his personal service.

sentences.zh: 郎柱爲部人所戕，其妻襁負幼子納穆泰於背，屬鞬佩刀，左右射，奪門出，以其族來歸。

translations.literal: Langzhu was killed by men of the tribe. His wife carried the infant Namutai on her back in swaddling clothes, hung a quiver and wore a sword, shot left and right, broke out through the gate, and came over with her clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Langzhu was murdered by fellow tribesmen, his wife strapped the infant Namutai to her back, slung a quiver and drew her sword, shot in every direction, fought her way out the gate, and led her clan to join the khan.

sentences.zh: 部人尋亦附太祖。

translations.literal: The people of the tribe soon also submitted to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the tribe soon submitted to Nurhaci as well.

sentences.zh: 揚古利手刃殺父者，割耳鼻生啖之，時年甫十四，太祖深異焉。

translations.literal: Yangguli personally killed his father's murderer, cut off his ears and nose, and ate them raw. He was then only fourteen, and Taizu was deeply astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Yangguli slew his father's killer with his own hand, cut off the man's ears and nose, and devoured them while they were still raw. He was only fourteen, and Nurhaci was deeply struck by it.

sentences.zh: 日見信任，妻以女，號爲「額駙」。

translations.literal: Day by day he gained trust; Taizu gave him a daughter in marriage and styled him "efu."
translations.idiomatic: He won increasing trust, was given a princess in marriage, and was styled an efu, an imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲正黃旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established, he was enrolled in the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were organized, he was assigned to the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 太祖令揚古利守汛鴨綠江，警備嚴密，無敢犯者。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Yangguli to guard the Yalu River frontier. His defenses were strict, and none dared violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Nurhaci posted Yangguli to guard the Yalu frontier. His precautions were so strict that no one dared cross it.

sentences.zh: 伐輝發多璧城，阻水不得進，揚古利亂流而濟，眾從之，遂薄城，多所俘馘。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Huifa at Duobi Castle, the army was blocked by water and could not advance. Yangguli crossed the current at random points; the troops followed, pressed the city, and took many captives and heads.
translations.idiomatic: During the attack on Huifa's Duobi Castle, the army was stopped by the river until Yangguli forded the swirling current; the men followed, closed on the city, and took many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳，略朱舍里路、訥殷路，戊戌，略安褚拉庫路，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the year guisi he raided the Zhusheli and Neyin routes; in wuxu he raided the Anzhulaku route, distinguishing himself in each.
translations.idiomatic: In guisi (1593) he raided the Zhusheli and Neyin routes; in wuxu (1598) he raided the Anzhulaku route, earning merit in both campaigns.

sentences.zh: 歲己亥，從克哈達，揚古利先登，擒貝勒孟格布祿。

translations.literal: In the year jihai he followed in the capture of Hada. Yangguli was first to mount the wall and seized the beile Menggebulu.
translations.idiomatic: In jihai (1599) he took part in the conquest of Hada, was first over the wall, and captured the beile Menggebulu.

sentences.zh: 歲丁未正月，徙蜚悠城眾，揚古利與扈爾漢率兵三百護行，烏喇以萬人要諸路。

translations.literal: In the first month of dingwei (1607), when the people of Feiyucheng were being relocated, Yangguli and Hurhan led three hundred men to escort them. Ula blocked the routes with ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of dingwei (1607), when the Feiyucheng population was being moved, Yangguli and Hurhan escorted them with three hundred men while Ula intercepted the roads with ten thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 揚古利勵眾曰：「吾儕平居相謂死於疾寧死於敵，此非臨敵時乎？」

translations.literal: Yangguli encouraged the troops, saying: "We ordinarily say we would rather die before the enemy than die of illness—is this not the moment to face the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: Yangguli rallied the men: "We always say we would rather die fighting than die in bed—isn't this the moment to prove it?"

sentences.zh: 持矛突陣，殺烏喇兵七，敵稍卻。

translations.literal: He took a spear and charged the formation, killing seven Ula soldiers, and the enemy drew back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He charged the enemy line with his spear, killed seven Ula soldiers, and forced them to give ground.

sentences.zh: 夾河相持，諸貝勒軍總至，大破之。

translations.literal: The two sides faced each other across the river; when the beiles' forces all arrived, they inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The armies faced off across the river until the beiles' forces gathered and routed the Ula army completely.

sentences.zh: 五月，從貝勒巴雅喇等伐渥集部，取赫席黑路，爲前鋒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he followed the beile Bayara and others in attacking the Woji tribe, took the Hexihei route, and served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he joined the beile Bayara and others against the Woji tribe, seized the Hexihei route, and led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 馬兒古里村人驚兵至，走負山，因攻據其山巔，馳下擊之，盡殲丁壯，俘子女以歸。

translations.literal: The people of Ma'erguli village, startled by the army's arrival, fled to the mountains. He attacked and seized the summit, then charged down and destroyed all the fighting men, taking women and children captive on the return.
translations.idiomatic: When the villagers of Ma'erguli fled to the hills at the army's approach, he stormed the heights, swept down on them, wiped out every able-bodied man, and brought back the women and children as captives.

sentences.zh: 九月，伐輝發，越栅二重，先入，奪其城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, in the campaign against Huifa, he crossed two lines of palisades, entered first, and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, campaigning against Huifa, he crossed two palisade lines, was first into the city, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 歲庚戌七月，從台吉阿巴泰等伐渥集部，略木倫路，克吳兒瑚麻村，望林中烟起，即馳赴之，往復者三，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of gengxu (1610) he followed the taiji Abatai and others against the Woji tribe, raided the Mulun route, and took the village of Wu'erhuma. Seeing smoke rise in the forest, he galloped toward it three times back and forth and took very many captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of gengxu (1610) he joined the taiji Abatai against the Woji, raided the Mulun route, and captured Wu'erhuma village. Spotting smoke in the woods, he rode to it three times over and brought back a great haul of prisoners and booty.

sentences.zh: 歲壬子九月，從討烏喇，攻金州城，城中迎射拒，揚古利冒矢攻克之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of renzi (1612) he followed the punitive expedition against Ula, attacked Jinzho city, and when the city met them with volleys of arrows, Yangguli braved the missiles and stormed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of renzi (1612), on the campaign against Ula, he assaulted Jinzho; when the garrison met them with arrow fire, Yangguli charged through the hail of shafts and took the city.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑正月，再討烏喇，揚古利先眾進戰。

translations.literal: In the first month of guichou (1613), on the second expedition against Ula, Yangguli advanced before the army to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of guichou (1613), on the second Ula campaign, Yangguli went ahead of the main force to engage the enemy.

sentences.zh: 攻青河，烏喇貝勒布占泰兵甚銳，太祖傳矢命諸將退，揚古利持不可，麾眾迫城，聚一隅疾攻，遂拔之。

translations.literal: Attacking Qinghe, the troops of the Ula beile Buzhan Tai were very sharp. Taizu sent an arrow-message ordering the generals to withdraw, but Yangguli objected, commanded the troops to press the city, concentrated on one corner with a swift assault, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinghe the Ula beile Buzhan Tai's troops fought fiercely. Nurhaci sent word by arrow for the generals to pull back, but Yangguli refused, drove the men up to the walls, concentrated the attack on one corner, and stormed the place.

sentences.zh: 天命四年三月，明經略楊鎬大舉來侵，總兵杜松等攻界凡，大貝勒代善等帥師禦之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Tianming (1619), the Ming grand coordinator Yang Hao launched a major invasion; the regional commanders Du Song and others attacked Jiefan, and the great beile Daishan and others led troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianming 4 (1619), the Ming grand coordinator Yang Hao invaded in force; regional commanders including Du Song attacked Jiefan, and the great beile Daishan led the army to meet them.

sentences.zh: 我軍屯吉林崖，明軍屯薩爾滸山，兩軍相薄，揚古利與貝勒阿巴泰等爭先赴敵，破其軍，松等皆戰死。

translations.literal: Our army encamped at Jilin Cliff; the Ming army encamped at Mount Sarhu. As the two armies closed, Yangguli and the beile Abatai and others vied to reach the enemy first, broke their army, and Song and the others were all killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces camped at Jilin Cliff and the Ming at Mount Sarhu. When the armies clashed, Yangguli and the beile Abatai raced each other to the front, shattered the Ming line, and Du Song and his colleagues were all killed.

sentences.zh: 是夕，明總兵馬林以兵至，營於尚間崖。

translations.literal: That evening the Ming regional commander Ma Lin arrived with troops and encamped at Shangjian Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening the Ming commander Ma Lin arrived and pitched camp at Shangjian Cliff.

sentences.zh: 翌旦，移兵往攻，太祖命被創者勿往，揚古利裹創繫腕，率十牛彔兵，憑高馳擊，林兵大潰。

translations.literal: At dawn the army moved to attack. Taizu ordered the wounded not to go, but Yangguli bound his wounds and tied them to his wrist, led ten niru of troops, charged down from the heights, and Lin's army was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they advanced to attack. Nurhaci told the wounded to stay behind, but Yangguli bandaged his injuries, strapped them to his wrist, led ten companies downhill in a charge, and routed Ma Lin's army completely.

sentences.zh: 七月，攻鐵嶺，遇蒙古貝勒介賽兵，擊破之，遂獲介賽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he attacked Tieling, met the troops of the Mongol beile Jiesai, defeated them, and captured Jiesai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, attacking Tieling, he defeated and captured the Mongol beile Jiesai.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，從太祖攻瀋陽，壕深塹堅，眾難之；

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year he followed Taizu in attacking Shenyang. The moat was deep and the ramparts strong, and the troops found it difficult;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year six he joined Nurhaci's assault on Shenyang. The moats were deep and the walls strong, and the men hesitated;

sentences.zh: 揚古利拔刀揮本旗兵先登，奪敵所植竹籤以阻軍者，遂克之。

translations.literal: Yangguli drew his sword, waved on his banner troops to mount first, seized the bamboo stakes the enemy had planted to block the army, and thus took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yangguli drew his sword, led his bannermen up first, tore out the bamboo stakes the defenders had planted to block the assault, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 進攻遼陽，復先登陷陣，破其步卒，奪河橋，與明兵戰於沙嶺，大敗之。

translations.literal: Advancing against Liaoyang, he again mounted first and broke the formation, routed their infantry, seized the river bridge, fought Ming troops at Shaling, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Liaoyang he again led the escalade, shattered the enemy formation, routed the infantry, seized the river bridge, and at Shaling delivered a crushing defeat to the Ming army.

sentences.zh: 遼陽既拔，太祖嘉其戰多屢受創，命位亞八貝勒，統左翼兵，授一等總兵官，誡勿更臨陣。

translations.literal: After Liaoyang was taken, Taizu praised him for fighting in many battles and repeatedly being wounded, ordered his rank to stand below the eight beiles, put him in command of the left-wing troops, appointed him a first-rank zongbing officer, and admonished him not to go into battle again.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liaoyang fell, Nurhaci praised his record of wounds earned in battle after battle, ranked him just below the eight beiles, gave him command of the left wing, made him a first-rank commander, and told him he must not expose himself in combat again.

sentences.zh: 十年，揚古利守耀州，明將毛文龍遣兵三百來攻，略城南蕎麥衝，揚古利率兵追擊，盡殲之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Yangguli guarded Yaozhou. The Ming general Mao Wenlong sent three hundred men to attack and plunder the buckwheat fields south of the city. Yangguli led troops in pursuit and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten, while Yangguli held Yaozhou, the Ming commander Mao Wenlong sent three hundred men to raid the buckwheat fields south of the city. Yangguli pursued and wiped them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 旋進三等公。

translations.literal: He was soon advanced to third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年九月，同阿山等捕逃人，至雅爾古，遇文龍所部越塞採葠者，擊殺九十六人，獲千總三及其從者十六人以還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Tiancong (1629), together with Ashan and others he pursued runaway bondservants to Ya'ergu, encountered men from Wenlong's command who had crossed the border to gather ginseng, killed ninety-six, and captured three chiliarchs and sixteen of their followers on the return.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tiancong 3 (1629), hunting fugitives with Ashan and others at Ya'ergu, he came upon Mao Wenlong's men gathering ginseng across the border, killed ninety-six of them, and brought back three chiliarchs and sixteen followers.

sentences.zh: 十月，從伐明，薄明都，擊敗滿桂兵於城北，礮兵陷敵伏中，揚古利率親軍十餘人奪圍入，悉出之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he followed the campaign against the Ming, pressed close to the Ming capital, and defeated Man Gui's troops north of the city. Artillerymen fell into an enemy ambush; Yangguli led a dozen or so of his personal guard to break in and bring them all out.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he joined the Ming campaign and closed on the capital, defeating Man Gui's force north of the city. When artillerymen were trapped in an ambush, Yangguli charged in with a dozen guards and rescued every one of them.

sentences.zh: 軍還，從貝勒阿巴泰等略通州，焚舟千餘。

translations.literal: On the army's return he followed the beile Abatai and others in raiding Tongzhou and burned more than a thousand boats.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he joined the beile Abatai in a raid on Tongzhou and burned more than a thousand vessels.

sentences.zh: 攻薊州，明軍來援，太宗督右翼三旗攻其西，貝勒代善等督左翼四旗攻其東，右翼兩紅旗兵少卻，揚古利率正黃旗兵直前突陣，敵敗走。

translations.literal: Attacking Jizhou, when Ming reinforcements came, Taizong personally directed the three right-wing banners against the west while the beile Daishan and others directed the four left-wing banners against the east. The two Red Banners on the right wing gave ground slightly; Yangguli led the Plain Yellow Banner straight forward in a charge and the enemy fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Jizhou, when Ming reinforcements arrived, Hong Taiji led the three right-wing banners against the west while Daishan led the four left-wing banners against the east. When the two Red Banners on the right wavered, Yangguli drove the Plain Yellow Banner straight into the enemy line and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 太宗命兩紅旗將佐納鍰自贖，以賜揚古利，揚古利分畀將士，不自私。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered the officers of the two Red Banners to pay silver in ransom for themselves and gave it to Yangguli, but Yangguli divided it among officers and soldiers and kept none for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji fined the Red Banner officers in silver and gave the sum to Yangguli, who distributed it among his men and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 六年，太宗伐察哈爾，命貝勒阿巴泰等及揚古利居守，明兵來侵，諸貝勒禦之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Taizong campaigned against the Chahar and ordered the beile Abatai and others and Yangguli to remain on guard. Ming troops invaded and the beiles repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In year six, while Hong Taiji campaigned against the Chahar, he left the beile Abatai and Yangguli to hold the home front. When Ming forces invaded, the beiles drove them back.

sentences.zh: 錦州戰，明兵銳甚，六旗俱卻，揚古利大怒，獨率本旗兵奮擊破之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Jinzhou the Ming troops were very sharp; six banners all fell back. Yangguli was furious and alone led his banner troops in a fierce assault that broke them.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinzhou the Ming fought fiercely and six banners gave ground. Enraged, Yangguli charged alone with his banner and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 旋復從太宗入明邊，攻大同、宣府，與貝勒阿巴泰等拔靈丘，隳王家莊，取之。

translations.literal: He soon again followed Taizong into the Ming borderlands, attacked Datong and Xuanfu, and with the beile Abatai and others took Lingqiu, destroyed Wangjiazhuang, and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Hong Taiji into Ming territory again, struck Datong and Xuanfu, and with the beile Abatai captured Lingqiu and destroyed and took Wangjiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，太宗諮諸將兵事，揚古利言：「用兵不可曠隔，若踰年不用，敵以其時乘間修備，慮誤我再舉。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year Taizong consulted the generals on military affairs. Yangguli said: "Warfare must not be left idle. If more than a year passes without use, the enemy will use the interval to repair their defenses, and I fear this will thwart our next campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year seven, when Hong Taiji asked his generals about strategy, Yangguli said, "Armies must not sit idle. If a year passes without action, the enemy uses the breathing space to strengthen their defenses and may spoil our next strike.

sentences.zh: 我暇，一年再征；

translations.literal: When we have leisure, campaign twice in a year;
translations.idiomatic: When we have time, campaign twice a year;

sentences.zh: 不暇，亦一年一征：乃爲善策。

translations.literal: when we lack leisure, at least once a year: that is the sound policy.
translations.idiomatic: when we are pressed, at least once— that is the sound policy.

sentences.zh: 我今當深入敵境克城堡，貝勒諸將已痘者駐守，未痘者從上還都。

translations.literal: I should now penetrate deep into enemy territory and take castles. Beiles and generals who have already had smallpox should remain on guard; those not yet infected should follow Your Majesty back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: We should now strike deep into enemy country and take fortified towns. Beiles and generals who have already had smallpox can stay to garrison; those who have not should return with Your Majesty to the capital.

sentences.zh: 不克，則縱兵焚其村聚；

translations.literal: If we do not take them, then let the troops burn their villages and hamlets;
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot take a place, burn the villages and hamlets;

sentences.zh: 民降者編伍，拒者俘以還。

translations.literal: people who submit should be enrolled in companies; those who resist should be taken captive and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: enroll those who surrender in our companies and bring back those who resist as captives.

sentences.zh: 各旗獻俘，視牛彔爲多寡，兵士所獲聽自取。

translations.literal: Each banner should present captives, with rewards apportioned by niru according to numbers; what soldiers capture they may keep for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Let each banner present captives and reward companies in proportion to their haul; let soldiers keep whatever they seize themselves.

sentences.zh: 若此，則人人貪得，不待驅迫，爭出私財買馬，兵氣益揚矣。

translations.literal: In this way everyone will be greedy for gain; without being driven they will vie to spend private wealth to buy horses, and military spirit will rise all the more.
translations.idiomatic: That way every man will hunger for loot, buy horses with his own money without being driven, and fighting spirit will only grow.

sentences.zh: 戍邊，貝勒許番代，他將卒不許番代。

translations.literal: On frontier garrison duty, beiles may be allowed rotation, but other officers and soldiers must not be allowed rotation.
translations.idiomatic: On frontier duty, beiles alone may rotate home; other officers and soldiers must not.

sentences.zh: 不耐勞苦，豈有能拓地成功業者乎？

translations.literal: If one cannot endure hardship, how can one expand territory and achieve success?
translations.idiomatic: Without enduring hardship, who can expand the realm and build an empire?

sentences.zh: 或謂用兵數，且妨農。

translations.literal: Some say frequent campaigning also hampers agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Some object that frequent campaigns will harm farming.

sentences.zh: 婦子相隨，且行且穫，何妨農之有？

translations.literal: Wives and children follow along, harvesting as they march—how does that hinder agriculture?
translations.idiomatic: Wives and children march with the army and harvest as they go—how does that harm the harvest?

sentences.zh: 朝鮮、察哈爾宜且置之，山海關外寧遠、錦州亦當緩圖，但深入腹地。

translations.literal: Korea and the Chahar should be set aside for now; beyond Shanhaiguan, Ningyuan and Jinzhou should also be taken slowly—only penetrate deep into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Leave Korea and the Chahar for later; beyond Shanhaiguan, defer Ningyuan and Jinzhou and strike deep into the interior instead.

sentences.zh: 腹地既得，朝鮮、察哈爾自來附矣。」

translations.literal: Once the interior is secured, Korea and the Chahar will submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Once the interior is ours, Korea and the Chahar will come over on their own."

sentences.zh: 時諸大臣所見亦略同，太宗遂定策伐明。

translations.literal: At the time the views of the great ministers were broadly similar, and Taizong thereupon decided on a policy of campaigning against the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The other ministers largely agreed, and Hong Taiji settled on a policy of war against the Ming.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，復錄揚古利前後戰功，進超品公，位亞貝勒，帽頂嵌珠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year his past and present battle achievements were again recorded; he was advanced to super-rank duke, ranked below the beiles, and his cap button was set with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year eight his whole record of service was reviewed again; he was raised to super-rank duke, placed just below the beiles, and given a pearl-studded cap button.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年五月，命武英郡王阿濟格，饒餘貝勒阿巴泰及揚古利帥師伐明，入邊，克畿內諸州縣凡十二城，五十八戰皆捷，獲總兵巢丕昌等，俘十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Chongde (1636), the Prince of Wuying Ajige, the Raoyu beile Abatai, and Yangguli were ordered to lead an army against the Ming. Entering the border, they took twelve cities and counties within the capital region; in fifty-eight battles all were victorious; they captured the regional commander Chao Pichang and others and took more than a hundred thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Chongde 1 (1636), Ajige, Prince of Wuying, the Raoyu beile Abatai, and Yangguli led a Ming campaign across the border, captured twelve towns and counties in the capital region, won fifty-eight engagements without a loss, took the commander Chao Pichang and others, and brought back more than a hundred thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 出邊，擊敗三屯營、山海關援兵。

translations.literal: On leaving the border they defeated the troops of Santunying and the Shanhaiguan reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: On the way out they defeated the Santunying garrison and the Shanhaiguan relief force.

sentences.zh: 九月，師還，太宗出都十里迎勞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army returned, and Taizong went ten li outside the capital to welcome and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, when the army returned, Hong Taiji rode ten li outside the capital to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 獻捷，設宴，親酌巵酒賜三帥。

translations.literal: They presented the victory report; a banquet was held, and he personally poured goblets of wine for the three commanders.
translations.idiomatic: They reported their victory at a feast where he personally poured wine for the three commanders.

sentences.zh: 十一月，論伐明諸將違律，阿濟格出邊不親爲殿，揚古利坐不睜，罰土黑勒威勒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, in reviewing violations of regulations by the generals in the Ming campaign, Ajige was charged with not personally commanding the rearguard on leaving the border, and Yangguli with failing to keep watch; both were fined tuhele weile.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, reviewing breaches of discipline on the Ming campaign, Ajige was fined for not commanding the rearguard in person on the withdrawal, and Yangguli for failing to keep proper watch—both paid tuhele weile penalties.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太宗親伐朝鮮，揚古利從。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Taizong personally campaigned against Korea, and Yangguli followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hong Taiji led a personal campaign against Korea, and Yangguli went with him.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，師濟漢江，屯江岸，朝鮮全羅、忠清二道兵來援，營漢城南。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the army crossed the Han River and encamped on the riverbank. Troops of Korea's Jeolla and Chungcheong circuits came to reinforce and encamped south of Hanseong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two the army crossed the Han and camped on its bank while Korean troops from Jeolla and Chungcheong circuits reinforced and pitched camp south of Seoul.

sentences.zh: 是月丁未，太宗命豫親王多鐸及揚古利擊之，值雪，陰晦，敵陣於山下，縱兵進擊，自麓至其巔，多鐸鳴角，招揚古利登山督戰。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of that month Taizong ordered the Prince of Yu Dodo and Yangguli to attack them. It was snowing and overcast; the enemy formed below the mountain. They loosed the troops in assault from the foot to the summit. Dodo sounded the horn to summon Yangguli up the mountain to direct the battle.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Hong Taiji sent Prince Dodo of Yu and Yangguli to attack them in snow and murk. The Koreans formed below the hill; our men fought from foot to summit. Dodo blew the horn calling Yangguli up the slope to direct the fight.

sentences.zh: 揚古利將馳赴，朝鮮敗卒伏崖側，竊發鳥槍，中揚古利，創重，遂卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: As Yangguli was about to gallop to them, defeated Korean soldiers lay in ambush beside the cliff, fired muskets in secret, struck Yangguli, and his wounds were grave; he died at once, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: As Yangguli spurred forward, defeated Koreans lying in ambush by the cliff fired muskets and hit him. His wounds were mortal; he died at once, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 明日，多鐸率兵逼敵營，朝鮮兵已夜遁，得揚古利尸以歸。

translations.literal: The next day Dodo led troops to press the enemy camp; the Korean army had already fled by night, and they recovered Yangguli's body and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Dodo advanced on the enemy camp; the Koreans had already fled overnight, and they recovered Yangguli's body.

sentences.zh: 太宗親臨哭奠，賜御用冠服以殯。

translations.literal: Taizong came in person to weep and offer sacrifices, and bestowed his own court robes and cap for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji came in person to mourn and sacrifice, and gave his own court robes and cap for the burial.

sentences.zh: 喪還，太宗迎於郊，命陪葬福陵。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession returned, Taizong welcomed it in the suburbs and ordered burial beside Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral cortege returned, Hong Taiji met it outside the city and ordered burial beside the Fuling mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 葬日，太宗復親奠。

translations.literal: On the day of burial Taizong again offered sacrifices in person.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day Hong Taiji sacrificed in person once more.

sentences.zh: 揚古利初事太祖，凡在行間，率先破敵，衝鋒挫銳，所向披靡。

translations.literal: From his first service under Taizu, whenever he was in the ranks he was first to break the enemy, charging to blunt their edge; wherever he turned, none could stand.
translations.idiomatic: From his first days with Nurhaci, Yangguli was always first to break the enemy line in battle; wherever he charged, nothing stood before him.

sentences.zh: 太宗誡不令臨陣，而遇敵忘軀，奮發不自已。

translations.literal: Taizong admonished him not to enter battle, yet when he met the enemy he forgot his body and could not restrain his ardor.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji forbade him to fight in the front line, yet whenever he met the enemy he forgot himself and could not hold back.

sentences.zh: 行軍四十餘年，大小百餘戰，功業絕特，而持身尤敬慎。

translations.literal: In more than forty years of campaigning he fought in over a hundred battles large and small; his achievements were singular, yet in personal conduct he was especially respectful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than forty years of campaigning and more than a hundred battles, his achievements were unmatched, yet in private life he was exceptionally restrained and careful.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗命本牛彔護軍爲之守門，賜豹尾槍二，以親軍二十人爲衞。

translations.literal: Taizong once ordered the guard troops of his own niru to guard his gate for him, gave him two leopard-tail spears, and made twenty personal guards his escort.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji once detailed the guards of his own company to watch Yangguli's gate, gave him two leopard-tail spears, and assigned twenty personal guards as his escort.

sentences.zh: 其葬，以本牛彔八戶守家。

translations.literal: At his burial, eight households of his niru were assigned to guard his house.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial, eight households from his company were assigned to guard his household.

sentences.zh: 是年十年一月，追封武勳王，立碑墓道。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Martial Merit and a stele was erected on the tomb road.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Martial Merit and a stele was raised on the tomb road.

sentences.zh: 順治中，世祖命配享太廟。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi reign the Shizu Emperor ordered him honored with sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi, the Shunzhi Emperor ordered him honored with a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十七年，聖祖巡盛京謁陵，親奠其墓。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi the Shengzu Emperor toured Shengjing to visit the tombs and personally offered sacrifice at his grave.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 37 (1698), the Kangxi Emperor toured Mukden to visit the tombs and personally sacrificed at Yangguli's grave.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，復建碑爲文表績。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year a stele was rebuilt with an inscription setting forth his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-nine a new stele was erected with an inscription recording his deeds.

sentences.zh: 雍正九年，定世爵爲一等英誠公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongzheng the hereditary rank was fixed as first-rank Duke of Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 9 (1731) the hereditary title was fixed as first-rank Duke of Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: 揚古利子二：長，阿哈旦，以軍功授拖沙喇哈番；

translations.literal: Yangguli had two sons: the elder, Ahadan, was appointed jasak for military merit;
translations.idiomatic: Yangguli had two sons: the elder, Ahadan, received the jasak rank for military merit;

sentences.zh: 次，塔瞻，襲超品公，擢內大臣。

translations.literal: the younger, Tazan, inherited the super-rank dukedom and was promoted to grand minister of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: the younger, Tazan, inherited the super-rank dukedom and was made a grand minister of the interior.

sentences.zh: 崇德六年八月，太宗親將禦明洪承疇，戰於錦州，敵遁，命塔瞻設伏追擊，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Chongde (1641), Taizong personally led troops against the Ming commander Hong Chengchou at Jinzhou. When the enemy fled, he ordered Tazan to set an ambush and pursue; many were beheaded or captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chongde 6 (1641), Hong Taiji personally led the army against Hong Chengchou at Jinzhou. When the Ming force fled, he had Tazan lay an ambush and pursue, killing and capturing a great number.

sentences.zh: 尋移營松山，明總兵曹變蛟夜率兵突近御營，塔瞻不能禦，降一等公。

translations.literal: Soon the camp moved to Songshan. The Ming regional commander Cao Bianjiao led troops by night in a sudden strike near the imperial camp; Tazan could not repel them and was reduced one rank in the dukedom.
translations.idiomatic: The army soon shifted camp to Songshan. When the Ming commander Cao Bianjiao raided the imperial camp by night, Tazan failed to repel him and was demoted one rank in the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，卒，以其子愛星阿襲，愛星阿自有傳。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi (1647) he died; his son Aisingga inherited, and Aisingga has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shunzhi 4 (1647); his son Aisingga succeeded him and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: =勞薩=勞薩，瓜爾佳氏，世居安褚拉庫。

translations.literal: Laosa. Laosa, of the Guwalgiya clan, had long resided at Anzhulaku.
translations.idiomatic: Laosa. Laosa belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and came from a family long settled at Anzhulaku.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐瓦爾喀部，取安褚拉庫，勞薩來歸。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against the Warka tribe and took Anzhulaku, Laosa came over.
translations.idiomatic: When Nurhaci campaigned against the Warka and took Anzhulaku, Laosa submitted.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established, he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were organized, he was assigned to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命六年，從伐明，克遼東，授游擊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianming (1621) he followed the campaign against the Ming, took Liaodong, and was appointed guerrilla colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 6 (1621) he joined the Ming campaign, helped conquer Liaodong, and was made a guerrilla colonel.

sentences.zh: 天聰二年，從伐蒙古多特羅部，進二等參將。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancong (1628) he followed the campaign against the Mongol Duotelo tribe and was advanced to second-rank brigade deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 2 (1628) he campaigned against the Mongol Duotelo tribe and was promoted to second-rank brigade deputy.

sentences.zh: 三年，從伐明，薄明都，與圖魯什等敗敵德勝門外，斬五十餘級，獲馬數十，進一等參將。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the campaign against the Ming, pressed close to the Ming capital, and with Tulushi and others defeated the enemy outside Desheng Gate, beheaded more than fifty, captured several dozen horses, and was advanced to first-rank brigade deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he joined the Ming campaign and closed on the capital; with Tulushi and others he defeated the enemy outside Desheng Gate, took more than fifty heads and dozens of horses, and was promoted to first-rank brigade deputy.

sentences.zh: 八旗選精銳為前鋒，號「噶布什賢」。

translations.literal: The Eight Banners selected elite troops as vanguard, styled "Gabsiheen."
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Banners picked elite troops for the vanguard, called the Gabsiheen.

sentences.zh: 勞薩驍勇善戰，使為將，號「噶喇依章京」。

translations.literal: Laosa was fierce and skilled in battle; he was made a commander and styled "Galai janggin."
translations.idiomatic: Laosa was a fierce fighter; he was made a commander with the title Galai janggin.

sentences.zh: 每出師，前行偵敵，所向有功。

translations.literal: On every campaign he went ahead to scout the enemy and distinguished himself wherever he turned.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign he rode ahead to scout the enemy and won merit wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，從伐明，圍大凌河城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year he followed the campaign against the Ming and besieged Dalinghe city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year five he joined the Ming campaign and besieged Dalinghe.

sentences.zh: 上聞明援兵自錦州至，遣勞薩與圖魯什以兵二百偵敵，上與貝勒多鐸以兵二百繼其後。

translations.literal: The khan heard that Ming reinforcements were coming from Jinzhou and sent Laosa and Tulushi with two hundred men to scout the enemy; the khan and the beile Dodo followed with two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Ming reinforcements were marching from Jinzhou, the khan sent Laosa and Tulushi with two hundred men to scout; he and Prince Dodo followed with another two hundred.

sentences.zh: 明兵至，逐勞薩等至小凌河，突近上前，上渡河躬陷陣，後軍亦至，共擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the Ming troops arrived they chased Laosa and the others to the Xiaoling River and suddenly pressed close to the khan. The khan crossed the river and personally entered the battle; the rear troops also arrived and together defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming pursued Laosa's party to the Xiaoling River and nearly reached the khan. He crossed the river and fought in person; when the rear guard came up, they routed the enemy together.

sentences.zh: 時我將覺善被圍，又有裨將與敵戰，敵揮刃將及，勞薩直前奮擊，悉拯之出，還，白上，上親酌金？

translations.literal: At the time our general Jueshan was surrounded, and a deputy commander was also fighting the enemy; the enemy's blades were about to reach him. Laosa charged straight forward and rescued them all. On returning he reported to the khan, and the khan personally poured him a golden cup.
translations.idiomatic: Our general Jueshan was surrounded and a deputy was locked in close combat with blades about to fall on him. Laosa charged in and rescued them all. When he reported back, the khan personally poured him a cup of gold.

sentences.zh: 以勞。

translations.literal: To reward his service.
translations.idiomatic: to reward his exertions.

sentences.zh: 明監軍道張春等合馬步兵四萬，渡小凌河，嚴屯拒戰，勞薩受上指，領纛而前，力戰破敵壘。

translations.literal: Ming army supervisor Zhang Chun and others combined forty thousand cavalry and infantry, crossed the Xiaoling River, and encamped in strict array to resist battle. Laosa, receiving the khan's instructions, led the standard forward and, fighting fiercely, broke the enemy stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun, the Ming army supervisor, mustered forty thousand horse and foot, crossed the Xiaoling River, and formed a tight camp to give battle. Acting on the khan's orders, Laosa took the banner and led the charge, breaking the enemy stockade in fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 十月，復與圖魯什往錦州松山偵敵，遇明兵，奔寧遠，斬其執纛者十餘人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he again went with Tulushi to scout the enemy at Jinzhou and Songshan. They met Ming troops fleeing toward Ningyuan and beheaded more than ten of their standard-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he again joined Tulushi to reconnoiter around Jinzhou and Songshan. They encountered Ming forces retreating toward Ningyuan and cut down more than ten of their standard-bearers.

sentences.zh: 十一月，聞察哈爾兵至，勞薩率兵百偵敵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, hearing that Chahar troops had arrived, Laosa led a hundred men to scout the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, when word came that Chahar troops were approaching, Laosa led a hundred men to scout them.

sentences.zh: 會察哈爾兵引去，追擊之，逾興安嶺，勿及，甲仗、駝馬委於道者，悉收以還。

translations.literal: When the Chahar troops withdrew, he pursued them over the Greater Khingan Range but could not overtake them. Armor, weapons, and camels and horses abandoned on the road were all gathered and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: The Chahar force pulled back, and he pursued them across the Greater Khingan Range but could not catch up. He collected all the armor, weapons, camels, and horses left along the road and returned with them.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，從伐察哈爾，師次博羅額爾吉，勞薩率兵前行，收蒙古流散者二百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year he followed the campaign against the Chahar. When the army halted at Boluo Erji, Laosa led troops forward and gathered more than two hundred scattered Mongols.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year six he joined the campaign against the Chahar. When the army encamped at Boluo Erji, Laosa pushed ahead and rounded up more than two hundred Mongols who had been scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 五月，與阿山率兵百至喀喇莽柰偵敵，遇察哈爾邏卒，逐而斬之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, with Ashan he led a hundred men to Karlamangnai to scout the enemy, met Chahar patrols, pursued them, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he and Ashan took a hundred men to scout at Karlamangnai, ran into Chahar patrols, chased them down, and killed them.

sentences.zh: 我國諜者劉哈為敵困，敵兵殆百人，勞薩以七騎大呼破圍入，挾之出，敵披靡敗走。

translations.literal: Our spy Liu Ha was trapped by the enemy, who numbered nearly a hundred. Laosa with seven horsemen broke the encirclement with a great shout, entered, carried him out, and the enemy scattered in defeat and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Our spy Liu Ha was surrounded by nearly a hundred enemy troops. Laosa charged in with only seven horsemen, shouting as he broke the ring, pulled Liu Ha out, and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 尋偵察哈爾汗棄地，遁已遠，還白上，上乃自布龍圖班師，至枯？

translations.literal: Soon afterward, scouting the Chahar khan's abandoned territory, he found the enemy had already fled far away. On returning to report to the khan, the khan then withdrew the army from Bulongtu and marched as far as Kuhe.
translations.idiomatic: He soon learned in scouting that the Chahar khan had abandoned his lands and was already far in flight. When he reported back, the khan withdrew from Bulongtu and marched the army to Kuhe.

sentences.zh: ，勞薩還與大軍會。

translations.literal: Laosa returned and joined the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Laosa then rejoined the main force.

sentences.zh: 七年，上命勞薩與圖魯什等將三百人略寧遠，分其兵兩翼突入沙河所，斬三百人，獲裨將一、牲畜二百七十。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the khan ordered Laosa, Tulushi, and others to lead three hundred men to raid Ningyuan. Dividing their forces on both wings, they burst into Shahe Station, beheaded three hundred men, and captured one deputy commander, two hundred and seventy head of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven the khan sent Laosa, Tulushi, and others with three hundred men to raid Ningyuan. Splitting into two wings, they stormed Shahe Station, killed three hundred men, and took one Ming deputy commander and two hundred seventy head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，复略錦州松山邊境，往錦州投書明總兵祖大壽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he again raided the Jinzhou-Songshan border and went to Jinzhou to deliver a letter to the Ming commander-in-chief Zu Dashou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year eight he again raided the Jinzhou-Songshan frontier and sent a letter to the Ming commander Zu Dashou at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，與圖爾格率兵出邊，渡遼河，沿張古台河屯戍，衛蒙古，扼明兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, with Turgene he led troops beyond the border, crossed the Liao River, and garrisoned along the Zhanggutai River to protect the Mongols and block the Ming army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he and Turgene took troops across the frontier, crossed the Liao River, and encamped along the Zhanggutai River to shield the Mongols and hold the Ming forces in check.

sentences.zh: 勞薩屢以寡勝眾，功多，進三等副將，賜號碩翁科洛巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Laosa repeatedly defeated larger forces with fewer men and achieved many feats. He was advanced to third-rank deputy commander and granted the title Suwengkolobaturu.
translations.idiomatic: Laosa repeatedly won victories against odds and piled up merit. He was promoted to third-rank deputy commander and given the honorific Suwengkolobaturu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，察哈爾部眾來歸，命勞薩將百人迎護。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, when Chahar tribesmen came over in submission, Laosa was ordered to lead a hundred men to meet and escort them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, when Chahar tribes submitted, he was ordered to lead a hundred men to meet and escort them in.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，從貝勒多爾袞收降察哈爾部眾，師還，略明邊，勞薩夜率兵進敗寧武關兵，遂毀關入，進略代州；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year he followed Prince Dorgon in receiving the surrender of Chahar tribesmen. When the army returned and raided the Ming border, Laosa by night led troops forward, defeated the Ningwu Pass garrison, destroyed the pass and entered, and advanced to raid Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year nine he followed Prince Dorgon in accepting the surrender of the Chahar. On the return march he raided the Ming frontier; Laosa led a night attack that routed the Ningwu Pass garrison, broke through the pass, and pushed on to raid Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 復進略忻州，度黑峰口，遇明邏卒四十人，悉擊斬之，獲其馬。

translations.literal: He again advanced to raid Xinzhou, crossed Heifeng Pass, met forty Ming patrols, struck and beheaded them all, and captured their horses.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to raid Xinzhou, crossed Heifeng Pass, encountered forty Ming scouts, killed them all, and seized their horses.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，偕吳松等齎書諭明松棚路潘家口諸戍將，因偵敵邊隘，多所俘馘​​。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he went with Wu Song and others bearing letters to instruct the Ming garrison commanders of Songpeng Road and Panjiakou, and while scouting the border passes took many captives and heads.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 (1636) he joined Wu Song and others in carrying letters to the Ming garrison commanders along Songpeng Road and at Panjiakou; while reconnoitering the passes he took many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 上伐朝鮮，命勞薩與戶部承政馬福塔以兵三百先為賈人裝，晝夜行，將至朝鮮，其戍將出禦，力戰，盡殪其眾。

translations.literal: When the khan campaigned against Korea, he ordered Laosa and Household Department commissioner Ma Futa to take three hundred men disguised as merchants and march day and night. When they were about to reach Korea, its garrison commander came out to oppose them. After fierce fighting they exterminated his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji marched on Korea, he sent Laosa and Household Commissioner Ma Futa ahead with three hundred men disguised as merchants, traveling day and night. As they neared Korea the local garrison commander came out to fight; after a hard battle they wiped out his entire command.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮國王李倧使勞師郊外，以其間走南漢山城。

translations.literal: The king of Korea, Li Jong, sent envoys to conciliate the army in the suburbs, and in the interval fled to Namhansanseong.
translations.idiomatic: King Li Jong of Korea sent envoys to treat with the army outside the city, then slipped away in the interval to Namhansanseong.

sentences.zh: 師還，吏議勞薩備不嚴，使倧得走，當奪世職論罰，上命毋奪職。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the officials judged that Laosa's defenses had not been strict enough to prevent Jong's escape and that his hereditary rank should be stripped and he should be punished. The khan ordered that his office not be taken away.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, the officials held that Laosa had not guarded tightly enough and had let Jong escape; they recommended stripping his hereditary rank and imposing punishment. The khan ordered that his office be retained.

sentences.zh: 二年，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he was made a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，從伐喀爾喀，上使勞薩齎書諭明宣府將吏歸歲幣、開巿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year he followed the campaign against the Khalkha. The khan sent Laosa bearing a letter instructing the Ming officials and officers of Xuanfu to restore the annual tribute and open the markets.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year three he joined the Khalkha campaign. The khan sent Laosa with a letter urging the Ming officials at Xuanfu to restore the annual payments and reopen trade.

sentences.zh: 勞薩獲喀爾喀四十餘人，收其財物、牲畜，縱使去。

translations.literal: Laosa captured more than forty Khalkha men, took their goods and livestock, and released them to go.
translations.idiomatic: Laosa seized more than forty Khalkha men, confiscated their goods and livestock, and then let them go.

sentences.zh: 師還，吏議勞薩罪當死，上特命宥之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the officials judged Laosa's offense merited death. The khan specially ordered that he be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, the officials ruled that Laosa deserved death. The khan personally pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 八月，從貝勒岳託、杜度伐明，自密雲牆子嶺口入。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he followed Princes Yueto and Dudu in campaigning against the Ming, entering through the Qiangziling Pass of Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he joined Princes Yueto and Dudu on a Ming campaign, entering through Miyun's Qiangziling Pass.

sentences.zh: 岳託奏言：「噶布什賢將領勞薩等逐潰兵，得明邏卒，诇知牆子嶺堅不易拔，嶺東西高處可越。」

translations.literal: Yueto memorialized: "The Gabsiheen commander Laosa and others chased fleeing troops and captured a Ming patrol, from whom they learned that Qiangziling is strongly held and hard to take, but the high ground east and west of the ridge can be crossed."
translations.idiomatic: Yueto reported: "Commander Laosa of the Gabsiheen and others ran down fugitives and caught a Ming scout who said Qiangziling was strongly held and hard to storm, but the heights east and west of the ridge could be crossed."

sentences.zh: 分軍四路深入，明兵合馬步八千人拒戰，阿蘭泰所將蒙古兵稍卻，勞薩與圖賴等奮戰陷陣，明兵敗去，其夜復至，勞薩擊卻之，遂入其壘；

translations.literal: The army was divided into four columns and advanced deep. Eight thousand Ming horse and foot combined to resist. The Mongol troops led by Alantai fell back slightly. Laosa and Tulei and others fought fiercely and broke the enemy lines. The Ming troops were defeated and withdrew, but returned that night. Laosa drove them back and then entered their stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The force split into four columns and pushed deep inland. Eight thousand Ming horse and foot stood to fight. Alantai's Mongols gave a little ground, but Laosa, Tulei, and the others fought their way into the enemy ranks. The Ming line broke and fell back, then returned that night; Laosa beat them off again and entered their camp.

sentences.zh: 又率所部逐敵，斬百七十餘級，俘九十，獲馬百三十有奇，進二等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: He again led his command in pursuit of the enemy, beheaded more than one hundred and seventy, captured ninety, seized more than one hundred and thirty horses, and was advanced to second-rank meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his own troops in pursuit, took more than one hundred seventy heads and ninety prisoners, and captured over one hundred thirty horses. He was promoted to second-rank meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，與吳拜偵敵廣寧邊境，自中後所入，循海而南，斬二百級。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, with Wubai he scouted the Guangning border, entered from Zhonghousuo, followed the coast southward, and beheaded two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year five he and Wubai reconnoitered the Guangning frontier, entered from Zhonghousuo, swept south along the coast, and took two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 上自將攻錦州，勞薩伏兵高橋，縱敵弗擊，論罪，降世職，奪賜號。

translations.literal: When the khan personally led the attack on Jinzhou, Laosa lay in ambush at Gaoqiao but let the enemy pass without striking. He was judged guilty, his hereditary rank was reduced, and his honorific title was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: During the khan's personal assault on Jinzhou, Laosa held an ambush at Gaoqiao but allowed the enemy to pass without attacking. He was found guilty, reduced in hereditary rank, and stripped of his honorific title.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗伐明，圍錦州，設伏，擊明兵松山，獲馬百九十。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year he followed Prince Jirhalang of Zheng in campaigning against the Ming, besieged Jinzhou, set an ambush, and struck Ming troops at Songshan, capturing one hundred and ninety horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year six he followed Prince Jirhalang of Zheng against the Ming, besieged Jinzhou, laid an ambush, and hit Ming forces at Songshan, seizing one hundred ninety horses.

sentences.zh: 勞薩逐明兵，見敵援至，使騎馳問濟爾哈朗曰：「敵援至，若之何？」

translations.literal: Laosa pursued the Ming troops and, seeing enemy reinforcements arrive, sent a rider galloping to ask Prince Jirhalang: "Enemy reinforcements have come—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: While pursuing the Ming, Laosa saw enemy reinforcements approaching and sent a rider to Prince Jirhalang asking, "Reinforcements are here—what should we do?"

sentences.zh: 濟爾哈朗以為怯，聞於上，上曰：「勞薩素勇敢，且身被重創，不當議小過。」

translations.literal: Jirhalang thought this cowardice and reported it to the khan. The khan said: "Laosa has always been brave, and he now bears serious wounds; one should not discuss minor faults."
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang took this for timidity and reported it to the khan, who said, "Laosa has always been fearless, and he is badly wounded besides; do not make much of a small lapse."

sentences.zh: 五月，明總督洪承疇以兵六萬援錦州，屯松山北，我師未集，勞薩力戰，敗其前鋒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Ming governor-general Hong Chengchou came with sixty thousand men to relieve Jinzhou and encamped north of Songshan. Our army was not yet fully assembled, but Laosa fought fiercely and defeated the enemy vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ming governor-general Hong Chengchou marched sixty thousand men to relieve Jinzhou and camped north of Songshan. Our forces were not yet gathered, but Laosa fought hard and routed the enemy vanguard.

sentences.zh: 會上命睿郡王多爾袞等濟師，復與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: When the khan ordered Prince Dorgon and others to bring up reinforcements, he again joined battle and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Once the khan ordered Prince Dorgon and others to bring up reinforcements, our troops engaged again and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 勞薩行塔山東偵敵，獲敵騎，克錦州外城。

translations.literal: Laosa went east of Tashan to scout the enemy, captured enemy horsemen, and took the outer wall of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Laosa scouted east of Tashan, seized enemy cavalry, and captured the outer wall of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，命复勞薩世職、賜號。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was ordered to restore Laosa's hereditary rank and honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the khan ordered Laosa's hereditary rank and honorific title restored.

sentences.zh: 旋代洪尼喀為梅勒章京。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he replaced Hungnike as meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He soon succeeded Hungnike as meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 是月，上自將督多爾袞等與承疇決戰，勞薩從多爾袞陷陣，力戰，死之。

translations.literal: That month the khan personally led and directed Dorgon and others in the decisive battle with Chengchou. Laosa followed Dorgon into the enemy lines, fought fiercely, and died.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the khan personally commanded Dorgon and the others in the final battle with Chengchou. Laosa followed Dorgon into the enemy ranks, fought to the end, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 既克敵，上遣內大臣攜酒臨奠，卹贈三等昂邦章京，以其子程尼襲。

translations.literal: After the enemy was defeated, the khan sent an inner minister bearing wine to offer sacrifice at his bier, posthumously granted third-rank angban janggin, and had his son Chengni succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory the khan sent an inner minister with wine to mourn at his bier, posthumously ennobled him as third-rank angban janggin, and had his son Chengni inherit the rank.

sentences.zh: 程尼既襲職，三遇恩詔，進一等伯，任議政大臣。

translations.literal: After Chengni succeeded to the office, he received three grace edicts, was advanced to first-rank baron, and served as deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chengni inherited the rank, received three grace edicts, rose to first-rank baron, and served as deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，從敬謹親王尼堪徵湖南。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Niken of Jingjin in campaigning against Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 (1652) he followed Prince Niken of Jingjin on the Hunan campaign.

sentences.zh: 十一月，及明將李定國戰於衡州，我師敗績，沒於陣，卹贈拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he fought the Ming general Li Dingguo at Hengzhou. Our army was defeated; he fell in battle and was posthumously granted the rank of tošaraha.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he met the Ming general Li Dingguo at Hengzhou. Our army was beaten and he died in the fighting; he was posthumously granted the rank of tošaraha.

sentences.zh: 十二年，追諡國初以來有功諸將，勞薩諡忠毅，程尼諡誠介，並立石紀績。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year posthumous titles were conferred on meritorious generals since the founding of the dynasty: Laosa was given the posthumous name Zhongyi, Chengni the name Chengjie, and stone monuments were erected to record their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve the court posthumously honored founding-era generals: Laosa received the temple name Zhongyi, Chengni received Chengjie, and stone monuments were raised to record their deeds.

sentences.zh: 勞薩弟羅壁，初以軍功授阿達哈哈番，至是並襲程尼世職，進為二等公。

translations.literal: Laosa's younger brother Luobi had first been granted the rank of adahaaha for military merit. At this time he also succeeded to Chengni's hereditary office and was advanced to second-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: Laosa's younger brother Luobi, who had earlier earned the rank of adahaaha in battle, now also inherited Chengni's hereditary office and was raised to second-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 卒，其子降襲一等伯。

translations.literal: When he died, his son succeeded at a reduced rank to first-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son inherited at a reduced grade as first-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 再傳，無嗣，乾隆間，續封二等子。

translations.literal: After two more generations the line died out; in the Qianlong reign a collateral branch was enfeoffed as second-rank viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later the line failed; in the Qianlong reign a collateral branch was re-enfeoffed as second-rank viscount.

sentences.zh: =圖魯什=圖魯什，伊爾根覺羅氏，世居葉赫。

translations.literal: Tulushi, of the Irgen Gioro clan, had long resided at Yehe.
translations.idiomatic: Tulushi belonged to the Irgen Gioro clan and came from a family long settled at Yehe.

sentences.zh: 歸太祖。

translations.literal: He submitted to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to Nurhaci.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established, he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were organized, he was assigned to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命九年，為。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianming he was made niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 9 (1624) he was appointed niru ejen, company commander.

sentences.zh: 擢甲喇額真，授？

translations.literal: He was promoted to jalan i ejen,
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to jalan i ejen,

sentences.zh: 牛錄額真。

translations.literal: and appointed jalan gashan commander.
translations.idiomatic: and given command as jalan gashan.

sentences.zh: 蒙古有亡者，逐得之。

translations.literal: When Mongols deserted, he pursued and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: When Mongols deserted, he hunted them down and brought them back.

sentences.zh: 十年，命率兵至旅順口捕盜，俘獲甚游擊世職。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to lead troops to Lüshunkou to capture bandits. He took very many captives and was granted the hereditary rank of guerrilla colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he was ordered to Lüshunkou to hunt down bandits. He captured a great many prisoners and was granted a hereditary guerrilla colonelship.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從太宗伐明，圖魯什先驅偵敵，至大安口，城下兵出戰，圖魯什單騎奮擊，師繼至，克之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he followed Taizong in campaigning against the Ming. Tulushi went ahead as vanguard to scout the enemy. Reaching Da'ankou, troops came out from below the city to fight. Tulushi charged alone on horseback; when the army came up, the place was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 (1629) he joined Hong Taiji on the Ming campaign. Tulushi rode ahead as vanguard scout. At Da'ankou the garrison sallied out; he charged alone, the main force came up, and the town fell.

sentences.zh: 自遵化向明都，明兵自薊州踵師後，圖魯什設伏擊卻之。

translations.literal: From Zunhua toward the Ming capital, Ming troops from Jizhou followed on the army's rear. Tulushi set an ambush and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Marching from Zunhua toward the Ming capital, he found Ming troops from Jizhou trailing the army. Tulushi laid an ambush and beat them off.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上軍明都西南，令圖魯什與梅勒章京阿山循城覘敵多寡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the khan encamped southwest of the Ming capital and ordered Tulushi and meiren janggin Ashan to circle the city and observe the enemy's numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the khan camped southwest of the capital and sent Tulushi and meiren janggin Ashan to ride around the walls and gauge the enemy strength.

sentences.zh: 獲諜，言明總兵滿桂、黑雲龍、麻登雲、孫祖壽合兵四萬，屯永定門南二里許。

translations.literal: They captured a spy who said the Ming commanders Man Gui, Hei Yunlong, Ma Dengyun, and Sun Zushou had combined forty thousand troops and were encamped about two li south of Yongding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They took a spy who reported that Ming commanders Man Gui, Hei Yunlong, Ma Dengyun, and Sun Zushou had massed forty thousand men about two li south of Yongding Gate.

sentences.zh: 還白上，且曰：「敵盛，宜及其不虞，乘夜擊之。」

translations.literal: On returning to report to the khan he also said: "The enemy is strong; we should strike while they are unprepared, attacking by night."
translations.idiomatic: Reporting back, he added, "The enemy is strong—we should hit them tonight while they do not expect it."

sentences.zh: 夜三鼓，秣馬蓐食，八旗及蒙古左、右翼兵俱進。

translations.literal: At the third watch of the night the horses were fed and the men ate at their bedding. The Eight Banners and the left and right wings of the Mongols all advanced.
translations.idiomatic: At the third watch the horses were fed and the men ate where they lay. The Eight Banners and the Mongol left and right wings all moved out.

sentences.zh: 圖魯什率所部先馳入敵壘，敵陣亂，師從之，明師遂敗，斬桂、祖壽，獲雲龍、登雲。

translations.literal: Tulushi led his command galloping first into the enemy stockade. The enemy formation was thrown into disorder; the army followed, and the Ming force was defeated. Gui and Zushou were beheaded; Yunlong and Dengyun were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Tulushi led his men in a headlong charge into the enemy camp. The Ming line collapsed, our troops poured in, and the Ming army was routed. Man Gui and Sun Zushou were killed; Hei Yunlong and Ma Dengyun were taken alive.

sentences.zh: 與勞薩、席爾納等往來游擊，屢有斬馘。

translations.literal: With Laosa, Xierna, and others he ranged back and forth in guerrilla raids and repeatedly took heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: With Laosa, Xierna, and others he ranged the field in mobile strikes and repeatedly took heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，從貝勒阿巴泰、濟爾哈朗逐斬叛將劉興祚，進二等參將。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he followed Princes Abatai and Jirhalang in pursuing and beheading the rebel commander Liu Xingzuo and was advanced to second-rank brigade deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year four he followed Princes Abatai and Jirhalang in running down and killing the rebel Liu Xingzuo and was promoted to second-rank brigade deputy.

sentences.zh: 既，復從貝勒阿敏守永平，諜告明兵且至，圖魯什以四十人偵之，巴篤理、屯布祿等以百人策應，共擊敗明別將張弘謨兵。

translations.literal: Afterward he again followed Prince Amin in defending Yongping. Spies reported that Ming troops were about to arrive. Tulushi scouted with forty men; Baduri, Tunbulu, and others supported him with a hundred. Together they defeated the Ming detached commander Zhang Hongmo.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Prince Amin in holding Yongping. When scouts warned that Ming troops were coming, Tulushi went out with forty men while Baduri, Tunbulu, and others backed him with a hundred. Together they routed the Ming detached force under Zhang Hongmo.

sentences.zh: 語詳巴篤理傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of Baduri.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Baduri.

sentences.zh: 已而，明兵大至，阿敏棄永平引師還。

translations.literal: Before long Ming troops arrived in force. Amin abandoned Yongping and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a large Ming force arrived. Amin abandoned Yongping and pulled the army back.

sentences.zh: 命往視邊牆，率兵五十為三隊，麾使後，獨與四騎先至塞下，蒙古數十人猝起，相薄兩垣間，環而射之，圖魯什突圍出，顧所將騎卒皆陷圍中，一騎中矢且僕，復大呼馳入，援三騎挾傷者俱歸。

translations.literal: He was ordered to inspect the border wall. Leading fifty men in three squads, he sent them to the rear and alone with four horsemen reached first below the pass. Several dozen Mongols suddenly rose, closed in between two walls, and surrounded them shooting. Tulushi broke out of the encirclement, but seeing that the horsemen he led were all trapped, and one horseman was wounded by an arrow and about to fall, he again shouted and galloped in, rescued three horsemen, and brought the wounded man back together.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to inspect the border wall, he divided fifty men into three squads, held the rest back, and rode ahead with only four companions to the foot of the pass. Several dozen Mongols sprang up between two walls and ringed them with arrows. Tulushi broke out, saw his men still trapped, and found one rider down with an arrow wound. He wheeled back with a shout, fought his way in again, and brought out three horsemen with the wounded man.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，從伐明，攻大凌河，明援兵二千自松山至，圖魯什與阿山、勞薩等以兵二百迎擊，敗之，斬百餘級，獲三纛。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year he followed the campaign against the Ming and attacked Dalinghe. Two thousand Ming reinforcements came from Songshan. Tulushi, with Ashan, Laosa, and others, met them with two hundred men, defeated them, beheaded more than a hundred, and captured three standards.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year five he joined the Ming campaign and assaulted Dalinghe. Two thousand Ming reinforcements marched from Songshan. Tulushi, Ashan, Laosa, and others met them with two hundred men, routed them, took more than a hundred heads, and seized three enemy banners.

sentences.zh: 還，上酌金？

translations.literal: On returning, the khan poured him a golden cup
translations.idiomatic: When they returned, the khan poured him a cup from a golden ewer

sentences.zh: 勞之。

translations.literal: to reward his service.
translations.idiomatic: to honor his exertions.

sentences.zh: 九月，攻錦州，明援兵自錦州至，與勞薩從上破敵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, attacking Jinzhou, when Ming reinforcements came from Jinzhou, he and Laosa followed the khan in defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, during the assault on Jinzhou, Ming reinforcements marched out from the city; he and Laosa followed the khan and helped rout them.

sentences.zh: 語詳勞薩傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of Laosa.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account appears in the biography of Laosa.

sentences.zh: 复遵上指，令軍中張旗幟，舉？

translations.literal: Again following the khan's instructions, he ordered banners displayed in the army and fired cannon,
translations.idiomatic: Again acting on the khan's orders, he had banners raised throughout the camp and cannon fired,

sentences.zh: ，偽若明兵來援，致城兵出戰，伏起，敵敗走。

translations.literal: feigning as if Ming troops were coming to relieve the city, so that the garrison came out to fight; when the ambush rose, the enemy was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: making it seem that Ming relief was arriving so the garrison would sally out; when the ambush sprang, the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 明監軍道張春等集諸路軍來援，渡大凌河，屯長山。

translations.literal: Ming army supervisor Zhang Chun and others gathered troops from various routes to relieve the city, crossed the Daling River, and encamped at Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun, the Ming army supervisor, assembled relief columns from several routes, crossed the Daling River, and encamped at Changshan.

sentences.zh: 圖魯什先以偏師邀擊，小胜。

translations.literal: Tulushi first intercepted them with a detached force and won a small victory.
translations.idiomatic: Tulushi first blocked them with a flanking detachment and won a minor victory.

sentences.zh: 戊戌之夕，上親督騎兵襲敵壘，圖魯什先進，兩軍力戰，卒破明師，獲張春。

translations.literal: On the evening of the day wuxu the khan personally directed the cavalry in a night assault on the enemy stockade. Tulushi advanced first. The two armies fought fiercely and finally broke the Ming force, capturing Zhang Chun.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of wuxu the khan personally led the cavalry in a night strike on the enemy camp. Tulushi went in first. After fierce fighting the Ming army was broken and Zhang Chun was captured.

sentences.zh: 十月，偵錦州松山，斬明兵執纛者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he scouted Jinzhou and Songshan and beheaded Ming standard-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reconnoitered Jinzhou and Songshan and killed Ming standard-bearers.

sentences.zh: 十一月，逐察哈爾兵，逾興安嶺。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he pursued Chahar troops over the Greater Khingan Range.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he chased Chahar troops across the Greater Khingan Range.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐察哈爾，次博羅額爾吉，招流亡，皆與勞薩偕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the campaign against the Chahar. When the army halted at Boluo Erji to gather refugees, all these actions were undertaken together with Laosa.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he joined the Chahar campaign. When the army paused at Boluo Erji to gather refugees, he did so alongside Laosa throughout.

sentences.zh: 上令哈爾佔具糧糗儲烏蘭哈達，而以甲喇額真顏布祿、牛錄額真董山司轉運，愆期，糧糗不時至，吏議當死。

translations.literal: The khan ordered Harzan to prepare provisions and store them at Ulanhada, while jalan i ejen Yanbulu and niru ejen Dongshan were put in charge of transport. They missed the deadline and provisions did not arrive on time. The officials judged that they deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: The khan ordered Harzan to prepare rations and store them at Ulanhada, with jalan i ejen Yanbulu and niru ejen Dongshan overseeing transport. They were late and supplies did not arrive on schedule. The officials ruled that they deserved death.

sentences.zh: 上命覆皆言法不當宥，圖魯什言：「曩者上申諭'臨陣而退當斬'，然亦嘗恩宥；

translations.literal: The khan ordered a review; all said that by law they should not be pardoned. Tulushi said: "Formerly the khan announced in instruction that 'retreating in battle merits execution,' yet pardon was also sometimes granted by grace;
translations.idiomatic: The khan ordered a review; every opinion held that the law allowed no pardon. Tulushi said, "Your Majesty once proclaimed that retreat in battle merits death, yet grace has sometimes spared men even so;

sentences.zh: 今罪顏布？

translations.literal: now if You punish Yanbulu
translations.idiomatic: now if You punish Yanbulu

sentences.zh: 讞，祿、董山而貸其死，實惟上恩。」

translations.literal: and Dongshan yet spare their lives, that will truly be Your Majesty's grace alone."
translations.idiomatic: and Dongshan yet spare their lives, that will truly be Your Majesty's grace alone."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The khan assented.
translations.idiomatic: The khan agreed.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，略錦州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he raided Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year eight he raided Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，擢噶布什賢噶喇依昂邦，進三等副將。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was promoted to gabsiheen galai angban and advanced to third-rank deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was raised to gabsiheen galai angban and promoted to third-rank deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 六月，復從伐察哈爾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he again followed the campaign against the Chahar.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he again joined the Chahar campaign.

sentences.zh: 七月，至歸化城，遇察哈爾諸宰桑以千二百戶來降，率以謁上。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, reaching Guihuacheng, he met Chahar chiefs bringing twelve hundred households to surrender and led them to audience with the khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, reaching Guihuacheng, he met Chahar chiefs bringing twelve hundred households to submit and led them before the khan.

sentences.zh: 是月，毀明邊牆入大同城，擊敗明總兵曹文詔？

translations.literal: That month they broke through the Ming border wall and entered Datong city, defeating Ming commander-in-chief Cao Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: That month the army breached the Ming border wall and entered Datong, defeating Ming commander Cao Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: ，與瑚什布等擊敗明總兵祖大弼軍，略地至宣化，攻懷遠，設伏左城西，使圖魯什如宣府偵敵。

translations.literal: With Hushibu and others he defeated the army of Ming commander-in-chief Zu Dabi, raided as far as Xuanhua, attacked Huaiyuan, set an ambush west of Zuocheng, and sent Tulushi toward Xuanfu to scout the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: With Hushibu and others he routed the army of Ming commander Zu Dabi, raided as far as Xuanhua, attacked Huaiyuan, laid an ambush west of Zuocheng, and sent Tulushi toward Xuanfu to scout.

sentences.zh: 閏八月乙酉，遇大弼偵卒十五人，圖魯什單騎馳？

translations.literal: On the day yiyou in the intercalary eighth month he met fifteen of Dabi's scouts. Tulushi charged alone on horseback into
translations.idiomatic: On intercalary eighth month, day yiyou, he encountered fifteen of Dabi's scouts. Tulushi charged alone on horseback into the

sentences.zh: 軍。

translations.literal: the enemy army.
translations.idiomatic: enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 上駐左擊，矢中其腹，猶力戰不已，斬二人，俘十三人。

translations.literal: He burst into the enemy formation; an arrow struck his belly, yet he fought on without cease, beheaded two men, and captured thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: He plunged into the enemy line. An arrow struck him in the belly, yet he kept fighting, killed two men, and took thirteen prisoners.

sentences.zh: 圖魯什創甚，上親迎視之。

translations.literal: Tulushi was gravely wounded. The khan personally went out to meet and inspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Tulushi was badly wounded. The khan went out in person to receive and tend him.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，卒於軍，賜號碩翁科羅巴圖魯，進三等總兵官。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai he died in the army. He was granted the title Suwengkorobaturu and advanced to third-rank commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On day dinghai he died in camp. He was granted the honorific Suwengkorobaturu and posthumously raised to third-rank commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 順治間，追諡忠宣。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi reign he was posthumously given the temple name Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi he was posthumously honored with the temple name Zhongxuan.

translations.literal: Bashitai, who succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Bashitai, who inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 子巴什泰，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Bashitai inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bashitai inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 事世祖。

translations.literal: He served Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: He served Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 三遇恩詔，進一等伯。

translations.literal: Three times he benefited from amnesty edicts and was advanced to first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: Three times favored by amnesty edicts, he rose to first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 順治九年三月，在上前為蒙古侍瑣尼所戕，進三等侯。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of Shunzhi, before the throne he was killed by a Mongol attendant; he was posthumously advanced to third-class marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Shunzhi 9 he was murdered before the emperor by a Mongol attendant and posthumously raised to third-class marquis.

sentences.zh: 子珠拉岱，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhuladai inherited [the rank].
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuladai succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，定封一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign his title was fixed as first-class jingkini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi the hereditary rank was fixed as first-class jingkini hafan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，改一等子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong it was changed to first-class viscount.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the title was revised to first-class viscount.

sentences.zh: =覺羅拜山=覺羅拜山，景祖弟包朗阿曾孫也。

translations.literal: =Jueluo Baishan= Jueluo Baishan was a great-grandson of Baolang'a, younger brother of Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: =Jueluo Baishan= Jueluo Baishan was a great-grandson of Baolang'a, the fifth younger brother of the dynastic ancestor Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 景祖兄弟凡六，分城而居，包朗阿次第五，居尼麻喇城。

translations.literal: Jingzu's brothers numbered six in all; each lived in his own walled settlement. Baolang'a ranked fifth among them and lived at Nimala City.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu had six brothers, each ruling his own fort. Baolang'a was the fifth and lived at Nimala.

sentences.zh: 太祖既起兵，族人惎太祖英武，謀欲害太祖，包朗阿子孫獨不與，率先事太祖。

translations.literal: Once Taizu had raised his army, clansmen envied Taizu's martial prowess and plotted to kill him; only Baolang'a's descendants did not join them and were first to serve Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Nurhaci raised arms, many kinsmen resented his prowess and plotted his death; only Baolang'a's line refused to join and was first to rally to him.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵之三年，攻哲陳部托漠河等五城，合兵戰於界凡，包朗阿諸孫札親、桑古里皆從。

translations.literal: In the third year after Taizu raised his army, he attacked five cities including Tuomohe of the Zhechen tribe. The combined forces fought at Gioro; Baolang'a's great-grandsons Zhajin and Sanguli all followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his uprising Nurhaci attacked five Zhechen towns including Tuomohe and fought at Gioro. Baolang'a's great-grandsons Zhajin and Sanguli both took the field.

sentences.zh: 拜山事太祖差後。

translations.literal: Baishan came to serve Taizu somewhat later.
translations.idiomatic: Baishan entered the khan's service later than the rest of his kin.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established, he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were organized he was assigned to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命六年，從太祖伐明，攻瀋陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianming he followed Taizu in campaigning against the Ming and attacked Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 6 he followed Nurhaci against the Ming and joined the assault on Shenyang.
