sentences.zh: 明將有？

translations.literal: Among the Ming generals there was one styled 'Bald-Tailed Wolf.'
translations.idiomatic: Among the Ming commanders was a fighter known as Bald-Tailed Wolf.

sentences.zh: 自城南來，拜山迎戰，斬副將一，遂降其？

translations.literal: Coming from south of the city, Baishan met them in battle, beheaded one deputy commander, and then received the surrender of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When they came up from the south of the city Baishan rode out to meet them, killed a deputy commander, and took their force intact.

sentences.zh: 號禿尾狼者，驍悍善戰，拜山殪諸陣。

translations.literal: Styled 'Bald-Tailed Wolf,' he was fierce and skilled in battle; Baishan killed him on the field.
translations.idiomatic: This Bald-Tailed Wolf fought with terrifying skill; Baishan cut him down in the thick of battle.

sentences.zh: 明兵悉。

translations.literal: The Ming troops were entirely subdued.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming force was wholly broken.

sentences.zh: 既克遼東，授游擊。

translations.literal: After Liaodong was taken, he was appointed guerrilla colonel.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong fell he was given the rank of guerrilla colonel.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從太宗伐明，攻錦州未下，移師攻寧遠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed Taizong in campaigning against the Ming. Jinzhou was attacked but not taken; the army shifted to attack Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 he followed Hong Taiji against the Ming. After failing to take Jinzhou the army turned on Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 錦州兵潛出躡師後，拜山與牛錄額真巴希競起還擊，戰死。

translations.literal: Jinzhou troops secretly came out and followed on the army's rear. Baishan and niru ejen Bashi both leapt up and counterattacked together; he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinzhou troops stole out and fell on the rear, Baishan and the company captain Bashi wheeled together to strike back—and Baishan was killed.

sentences.zh: 太宗親臨其喪，酹酒哭之，賜人戶、牲畜，贈三等副將。

translations.literal: Taizong personally attended his funeral, poured libation and wept for him, granted households and livestock, and posthumously gave him third-rank brigade deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji came in person to his funeral, poured wine and wept, granted households and livestock, and posthumously made him a third-rank brigade deputy.

sentences.zh: 子顧納岱，襲。

translations.literal: His son Gunadai inherited [the rank].
translations.idiomatic: His son Gunadai succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 顧納岱既襲職，天聰八年，改三等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: After Gunadai had inherited the post, in the eighth year of Tiancong it was changed to third-rank meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gunadai had succeeded, his office was revised in Tiancong 8 to third-rank meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，從伐明，戰於山海關，敗明兵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he followed the campaign against the Ming, fought at Shanhaiguan, and defeated Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 he joined the attack on the Ming, fought at Shanhaiguan, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 逐敵至豐潤，師或出採薪，明兵起乘之，顧納岱馳赴奮擊，援以歸。

translations.literal: Pursuing the enemy to Fengrun, when troops went out to gather firewood Ming soldiers rose and seized the chance. Gunadai galloped to the rescue, fought fiercely, and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the pursuit to Fengrun some men went out for firewood; when Ming troops struck, Gunadai galloped to their aid, drove the enemy back, and escorted his comrades home.

sentences.zh: 徇山東，擊敗明內監馮永盛、總兵侯應祿，克博平，進一等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: Sweeping through Shandong, he defeated the Ming eunuch Feng Yongsheng and regional commander Hou Yinglu, took Boping, and was advanced to first-rank meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning through Shandong he defeated the eunuch Feng Yongsheng and the regional commander Hou Yinglu, captured Boping, and rose to first-rank meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，顧納岱以擺牙喇纛章京從睿親王多爾袞入關擊李自成。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, Gunadai followed Prince Regent Dorgon through the pass to strike Li Zicheng as baiduhai commander of the banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 Gunadai followed Dorgon through the passes as a baiduhai banner commander to fight Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 十月，從豫親王多鐸逐自成至陝州，賊依山為陣，顧納岱與圖賴率擺牙喇兵馳擊，斬獲大半。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he followed Prince Dodo in pursuing Zicheng to Shaanzhou. The bandits formed their battle line on the hills. Gunadai and Turgut led baiduhai troops in a galloping attack and killed or captured more than half of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he followed Dodo in chasing Zicheng to Shaanzhou. When the rebels drew up on the hills Gunadai and Turgut led the baiduhai in a headlong charge and cut down more than half the enemy.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，自成將劉元亮以千餘人夜覘我師，顧納岱出擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Zicheng's commander Liu Yuanliang came with more than a thousand men by night to spy on our army; Gunadai went out, attacked, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shunzhi 2, Zicheng's general Liu Yuanliang brought a thousand men to reconnoiter by night. Gunadai sallied forth and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 鑲黃、正藍、正白三旗兵繼進，賊大奔，遂克潼關，逼西安，加半個前程。

translations.literal: Troops of the Bordered Yellow, Plain Blue, and Plain White banners advanced in succession. The bandits fled in great disorder. Tongguan was then taken and Xi'an pressed; he received an additional half seniority stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The Bordered Yellow, Plain Blue, and Plain White banners pressed forward; the rebels broke and ran. Tongguan fell, Xi'an was threatened, and Gunadai received an extra half stipend of seniority.

sentences.zh: 三月，從豫親王徇河南，渡淮。

translations.literal: In the third month he followed Prince Dodo in sweeping Henan and crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he followed Dodo across Henan and the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 四月，至揚州，與伊爾都齊等率擺牙喇兵軍於城南，獲舟二百餘。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the army reached Yangzhou. With Erduqi and others he led baiduhai troops and encamped south of the city, capturing more than two hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they reached Yangzhou. With Erduqi and others Gunadai camped south of the city with the baiduhai and seized more than two hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 翌日，合師薄城下，七日而拔。

translations.literal: The next day the combined forces pressed close beneath the walls; in seven days the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the combined armies closed on the walls; seven days later the city fell.

sentences.zh: 進克明南都，溯江至蕪湖，擊明將黃得功，敗其舟師。

translations.literal: Advancing he took the Southern Ming capital, went upriver to Wuhu, struck the Ming commander Huang Degong, and defeated his river flotilla.
translations.idiomatic: The army pushed on to take Nanjing, ascended the Yangtze to Wuhu, fought the Ming commander Huang Degong, and smashed his fleet.

sentences.zh: 移師從貝勒博洛徇蘇州，克崑山，攻江陰，發？

translations.literal: The army shifted to follow Prince Bolo in sweeping Suzhou, took Kunshan, and attacked Jiangyin, firing cannon to breach the walls,
translations.idiomatic: The army then followed Prince Bolo into Suzhou, took Kunshan, and besieged Jiangyin, where cannon fire broke the walls,

sentences.zh: 破城，顧納岱先登。

translations.literal: the city was broken, and Gunadai was first to climb up.
translations.idiomatic: and Gunadai was the first over the ramparts when the city gave way.

sentences.zh: 复移師趨浙江，略平湖，水陸並勝，收其戰艦。

translations.literal: Again shifting the army toward Zhejiang, he overran Pinghu, won on land and water together, and seized their warships.
translations.idiomatic: The army turned toward Zhejiang, overran Pinghu, won by land and water alike, and captured enemy warships.

sentences.zh: 攻嘉興，明兵出禦，背城為陣，顧納岱與固山額真恩格圖、漢岱等合擊之，三戰三勝。

translations.literal: Attacking Jiaxing, when Ming troops came out to resist and formed their battle line with the city at their backs, Gunadai together with gushan i ejen Enggu, Handai, and others combined in attack; three battles brought three victories.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiaxing the Ming came out to fight with their backs to the walls. Gunadai, Enggu, Handai, and others struck together—and won three times in three fights.

sentences.zh: 七月，師還，進三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the army returned and he was advanced to third-rank angban janggin.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned in the seventh month he was raised to third-rank angban janggin.

sentences.zh: 四年，從豫親王徵蘇尼特部，討騰機思，騰機思走喀爾喀，分遣蒙古兵追擊，敗之於歐特克山；

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Prince Dodo in campaigning against the Sunite tribes and punishing Tenggis. Tenggis fled to the Khalkha; detachments of Mongol troops were sent in pursuit and defeated the enemy at Otek Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Dodo against the Sunites to punish Tenggis. When Tenggis fled to the Khalkha, Mongol detachments were sent after him and crushed him at Mount Otek;

sentences.zh: 復自土喇河西行，敗喀爾喀兵於查濟布喇克。

translations.literal: again from west of the Tola River going west, he defeated Khalkha troops at Zhajibulak.
translations.idiomatic: then marched west of the Tola and routed Khalkha forces at Zhajibulak.

sentences.zh: 尋以恩詔進二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: Soon, by an amnesty edict, he was advanced to second-rank jingkini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward an amnesty edict raised him to second-rank jingkini hafan.

sentences.zh: 五年，從征南將軍譚泰下江西，討金聲桓，至九江，擊破聲桓兵；

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed the southern expedition commander Tan Tai down into Jiangxi to suppress Jin Shenghuan. Reaching Jiujiang, he smashed Shenghuan's troops;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Tan Tai into Jiangxi against Jin Shenghuan, reached Jiujiang, and shattered the rebel army;

sentences.zh: 進攻南昌，中砲，沒於陣。

translations.literal: advancing to attack Nanchang, he was struck by cannon and died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: then died in the assault on Nanchang when a cannonball found him.

sentences.zh: 贈一等精奇尼哈番，以其子莫洛渾襲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given first-rank jingkini hafan, and his son Moluohun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made first-rank jingkini hafan, and his son Moluohun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 莫洛渾授參領。

translations.literal: Moluohun was appointed company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Moluohun was made a company commander.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年，從安南將軍達素徇福建，討鄭成功，攻？

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi he followed General of Annam Daisu in sweeping Fujian to suppress Zheng Chenggong and assault Xiamen,
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 he followed Daisu into Fujian against Zheng Chenggong and led the attack on Xiamen,

sentences.zh: 門，死之。

translations.literal: and died there.
translations.idiomatic: and was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 聖祖以拜山、顧納岱、莫洛渾三世死王事，贈莫洛渾三等伯，諡剛勇。

translations.literal: Sheng Zu, because Baishan, Gunadai, and Moluohun for three generations died in the ruler's service, posthumously granted Moluohun third-class baron with the posthumous title Gangyong.
translations.idiomatic: Because Baishan, Gunadai, and Moluohun had given their lives in three generations, Kangxi posthumously made Moluohun a third-class baron with the posthumous name Gangyong, "Steadfast and Brave."

sentences.zh: 太祖始起，諸族人未附，有龍敦者，為景祖第三兄索長阿子，於太祖為從叔，撓太祖尤力。

translations.literal: When Taizu first rose, clansmen had not yet submitted. There was one Longdun, son of Suochanga, Jingzu's third elder brother and Taizu's paternal uncle, who obstructed Taizu with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: When Nurhaci first rose, his clansmen had not yet rallied. One Longdun—son of Suochanga, third elder brother of Jingzu and Nurhaci's uncle—worked hardest to thwart him.

sentences.zh: 太祖討尼堪外蘭、討李岱，漏師期，又構太祖異母弟薩木佔殺噶哈善哈思虎，皆龍敦所為也。

translations.literal: When Taizu punished Nikhan Wailan and punished Li Dai, [Longdun] leaked battle dates; again he incited Taizu's younger half-brother Samuzhan to kill Gahashan and Hasihu—all were Longdun's doing.
translations.idiomatic: He leaked campaign schedules during Nurhaci's punitive raids on Nikhan Wailan and Li Dai, and set Nurhaci's half-brother Samuzhan to murder Gahashan and Hasihu—all his handiwork.

sentences.zh: 然其從子旺善事太祖。

translations.literal: Yet his nephew Wangshan served Taizu well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nephew Wangshan remained loyal to Nurhaci.

sentences.zh: 太祖再攻兆佳城，取寧古親，旺善為敵踣，敵俯撲，出刃將刺；

translations.literal: When Taizu again attacked Zhaojia City and took Ningguzhan, Wangshan was knocked down by the enemy. An enemy leaned over and lunged, drawing his blade to stab;
translations.idiomatic: In Nurhaci's second assault on Zhaojia, when Ningguzhan was taken Wangshan was thrown by the enemy. A foe leaned over him, blade drawn to finish the kill;

sentences.zh: 太祖未及甲，直入發矢，中敵額，殪，援旺善起。

translations.literal: Taizu had not yet donned armor; he charged in and loosed an arrow, striking the enemy in the forehead and killing him, then lifted Wangshan up.
translations.idiomatic: Nurhaci had not yet armored himself. He rode straight in, put an arrow through the man's forehead, and hauled Wangshan to his feet.

sentences.zh: 其後屢從征伐。

translations.literal: Afterward he repeatedly followed in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in many campaigns thereafter.

sentences.zh: 天命十年，偕達珠瑚、。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianming, together with Dazhuhu and Che'erge,
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 10, together with Dazhuhu and Che'erge,

sentences.zh: 上出郊迎之，行抱見禮，慰諭甚至。

translations.literal: the khan went out beyond the suburbs to meet them, performed the embrace-and-audience rite, and comforted and instructed them with great earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: the khan rode out to meet them, honored them with the embrace rite, and spoke to them with exceptional warmth.

translations.literal: with fifteen hundred men they attacked the Warka tribe and captured a very great number.
translations.idiomatic: they took fifteen hundred men against the Warka and returned laden with captives.

sentences.zh: 車爾格，以千五百人伐瓦爾喀部，俘獲甚

translations.literal: Che'erge, with fifteen hundred men, attacked the Warka tribe; captives taken were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Che'erge led fifteen hundred men against the Warka and brought back a great haul of prisoners.

sentences.zh: 太祖既盛強，龍敦子鐸弼、托博輝皆從。

translations.literal: Once Taizu had grown mighty, Longdun's sons Duobi and Tuobohui both followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Nurhaci's power was fully established, Longdun's sons Duobi and Tuobohui both entered his service.

sentences.zh: 天命七年，太祖伐明，使鐸弼與貝和齊、蘇把海留守遼陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianming, when Taizu campaigned against the Ming, he sent Duobi with Bei Heqi and Subuhai to remain and garrison Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 7, during the campaign against the Ming, he left Duobi with Bei Heqi and Subuhai to hold Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，設八大臣，以托博輝領正藍旗。

translations.literal: When Taizong first acceded, he established eight great ministers and put Tuobohui in charge of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji first took the throne he appointed eight grand ministers and made Tuobohui head of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 又有土穆布祿，為景祖幼弟寶實諸孫。

translations.literal: There was also Tumublu, a grandson of Jingzu's youngest brother Baoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Another was Tumublu, a grandson of Jingzu's youngest brother Baoshi.

sentences.zh: 十年，命與阿爾代、毛海、光石等屯耀州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered with Erdai, Maohai, Guangshi, and others to garrison Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was posted with Erdai, Maohai, Guangshi, and others to garrison Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗設十六大臣，使與薩璧翰為托博輝佐。

translations.literal: When Taizong established sixteen great ministers, he had him and Sabihan assist Tuobohui.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji expanded the council to sixteen ministers, he and Sabihan were made Tuobohui's deputies.

sentences.zh: 又有郎球、巴哈納，皆索長阿之裔，俱致通顯，自有傳。

translations.literal: There were also Langqiu and Bahana, all descendants of Suochanga; each attained high eminence and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Langqiu and Bahana too were Suochanga's descendants; each rose to high office and receives his own biography.

sentences.zh: 太祖，授扎爾固齊？

translations.literal: [He] served Taizu and was appointed jarguci.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Nurhaci's service and was made a jarguci.

sentences.zh: 西喇布，世居完顏，以地為氏。

translations.literal: Xilabu had long resided at Wanyan and took the place as his clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Xilabu came from a line long settled at Wanyan and took that place as the family name.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起兵，率所部來歸，常翼。

translations.literal: When Taizu first raised his army, he led his command to submit and constantly flanked [the khan].
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Nurhaci's uprising he brought his followers over and kept constant guard at the khan's side.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳，略富爾佳齊，哈達人西忒庫抽矢射貝勒巴雅拉，西喇布以身當之，中二矢，遂卒，卹贈游擊。

translations.literal: In the year guisi, when overrunning Fuerjiaqi, a Hadah man Xitekü drew his bow and shot at Prince Bayara; Xilabu shielded him with his body, was struck by two arrows, and then died. He was mourned and posthumously granted guerrilla colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In guisi, during the raid on Fuerjiaqi, a Hadah archer named Xitekü shot at Prince Bayara. Xilabu threw himself in the way, took two arrows, and died. He was mourned and posthumously made guerrilla colonel.

sentences.zh: 子二：噶祿、馬喇希。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Galu and Malaxi.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Galu and Malaxi.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established, [the family] was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the banners were organized they were assigned to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 噶祿襲職，從攻沙嶺有功，進二等參將。

translations.literal: Galu inherited the post. Following the attack on Shaling he had merit and was advanced to second-rank brigade deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Galu succeeded to the title and earned distinction at Shaling, rising to second-rank brigade deputy.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without a son.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving no son.

sentences.zh: 馬喇希，天聰九年，授佐領。

translations.literal: Malaxi, in the ninth year of Tiancong, was appointed company assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: Malaxi received a company assistant command in Tiancong 9.

sentences.zh: 尋襲其兄噶祿世職。

translations.literal: Soon he inherited his elder brother Galu's hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon succeeded to his brother Galu's hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 崇德二年，從都統葉克舒等伐卦勒察。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongde he followed military governor Yekeshu and others in campaigning against the Gualicha.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 2 he joined Yekeshu's campaign against the Gualicha.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，授刑部理事官。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year he was appointed a minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chongde 3 he became a minister of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 八月，遷蒙古梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to Mongol meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was transferred to Mongol meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 四年，再遷固山額真。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred again to gushan i ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted again to gushan ejen.

sentences.zh: 從睿親王多爾袞圍錦州，坐徇王貝勒等私遣兵歸，離城遠駐，罰如律。

translations.literal: Following Prince Regent Dorgon in besieging Jinzhou, he was punished according to law for indulging princes and beile in privately sending troops home and encamping far from the city.
translations.idiomatic: During Dorgon's siege of Jinzhou he was fined under law for winking at princes who sent men home and camped too far from the walls.

sentences.zh: 復從貝勒阿巴泰等入黃崖口，所至克捷。

translations.literal: Again following Prince Abatai and others through Huangyakou, wherever they went they achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Abatai through Huangyakou afterward and won at every turn.

sentences.zh: 順治元年四月，從睿親王多爾袞入關破李自成，追擊至慶都。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Regent Dorgon through the pass, broke Li Zicheng, and pursued him to Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 1 he followed Dorgon through the passes, routed Li Zicheng, and chased him to Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，與都統阿山徵陝西，自蒲州渡河擊賊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, together with military governor Ashan, he campaigned in Shaanxi, crossed the river from Puzhou, and struck the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he joined Ashan in the Shaanxi campaign, forded the Yellow River at Puzhou, and struck the rebels.

sentences.zh: 論功，進一等甲喇章京兼半個前程。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed he was advanced to first-rank jalan janggin with an additional half seniority stipend.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was raised to first-rank jalan janggin with an extra half stipend of seniority.

sentences.zh: 尋命移師從豫親王多鐸下江南。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to shift the army and follow Prince Dodo south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered south with Dodo below the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，自歸德渡河至泗北淮河橋，明守將焚橋走，師夜濟，與都統宗室拜音圖以紅衣砲攻克武岡寨，引兵而東。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, from Guide he crossed the river to the Huaihe Bridge north of Si. The Ming defending commander burned the bridge and fled; the army crossed by night. With the imperial clansman and military governor Baiyintu he used red-coated cannon to take Wugangzhai and led the troops east.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Shunzhi 2 he crossed from Guide to the Huai River bridge north of Si. When the Ming commander burned the bridge and fled, the army crossed by night. With Baiyintu he took Wugang Stockade with red-barreled cannon and marched east.

sentences.zh: 至常州，明將黃蜚以步兵數万禦戰，擊破之，遂下宜興，道破明水軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Changzhou, the Ming commander Huang Fei opposed the battle with tens of thousands of foot soldiers; he was defeated and broken, and Yixing was then taken. On the road he smashed the Ming river force.
translations.idiomatic: At Changzhou he broke Huang Fei and ten thousand foot soldiers, took Yixing, and along the way destroyed the Ming river force.

sentences.zh: 至崑山，都統恩格圖等方攻城，馬喇希率所部兵趨頹堞，先登，遂克之，复拔常熟。

translations.literal: Reaching Kunshan, while military governor Enggu and others were just attacking the city, Malaxi led his command toward a crumbling parapet, climbed first, and then took it; he again captured Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: At Kunshan, while Enggu was still battering the walls, Malaxi led his men to a crumbling breach, was first over, and took the city—then seized Changshu as well.

sentences.zh: 師還，進三等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was advanced to third-rank meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was raised to third-rank meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，從肅親王豪格徇陝西，至漢中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year he followed Prince Suha in sweeping Shaanxi and reached Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Shunzhi 4 he followed Suha into Shaanxi as far as Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 叛將賀珍走西鄉，馬喇希與都統鰲拜分兵，進二等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: The rebel commander He Zhen fled to Xixiang. Malaxi and military governor Oboi divided their forces, galloped in pursuit as far as Chu and Hu, and killed or captured a great many; he was advanced to second-rank ashan-i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel He Zhen fled to Xixiang, Malaxi and Oboi split their forces, chased him through Chu and Hu, and took a great toll of heads—earning Malaxi promotion to second-rank ashan-i hafan.

sentences.zh: 五年，睿親王多爾袞出獵，馬喇希坐？

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Prince Regent Dorgon went hunting, Malaxi was punished for
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, while Dorgon was out hunting, Malaxi was punished for

sentences.zh: 馳擊，及於楚、湖，斬馘甚與都統噶達渾等私獵，貶秩。

translations.literal: private hunting with military governor Gadahun and others and was demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: going on unauthorized hunts with Gadahun and other generals and was reduced in rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖親政，詔復職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Shizu personally took power, an edict restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Shunzhi took personal rule, an edict restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 再遇恩詔，進三等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: Again benefiting from an amnesty edict, he was advanced to third-rank jingkini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Favored again by an amnesty edict, he rose to third-rank jingkini hafan.

sentences.zh: 九年九月，命與定南將軍、護軍統領阿爾津帥師定廣東。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year he was ordered with the Pacifier of the South, banner general Altin, to command the army and settle Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Shunzhi 9 he was ordered with Altin, the Pacifier of the South, to bring Guangdong under control.

sentences.zh: 十月，命移軍鎮漢中。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was ordered to shift the army to garrison Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month his troops were reassigned to garrison Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，復命移軍定湖廣辰州、常德諸路。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was again ordered to shift the army to settle the routes of Chenzhou and Changde in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was ordered to move again and pacify Chenzhou, Changde, and the other routes of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 十二年，世祖命追錄國初以來有功諸將，皆視一品大臣，予諡，立碑墓道，於是西喇布諡順壯，馬喇希諡忠僖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Shizu ordered that meritorious generals since the founding be posthumously recorded; all were treated as first-rank grand ministers, granted posthumous titles, and given steles at their tomb roads. Thereupon Xilabu was posthumously titled Shunzhuang and Malaxi Zhongxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Shunzhi Emperor ordered a retrospective honor roll of founding generals: each was treated as a first-rank minister, given a posthumous title, and granted a stele at the tomb road. Xilabu received the title Shunzhuang and Malaxi Zhongxi.

sentences.zh: 太祖諸將，當帝業未成，？

translations.literal: Among Taizu's generals, while the imperial enterprise was not yet established, many
translations.idiomatic: Among Nurhaci's generals, while the dynasty was still being forged, many

sentences.zh: 死行間，與西喇布同時易名紀績者，又有扎爾固齊阿蘭珠、梅勒額真納爾察。

translations.literal: died on campaign. Those remembered by posthumous titles at the same time as Xilabu also included the jarguci Alanzhu and the meiren ejen Na'ercha.
translations.idiomatic: fell on campaign. Others honored in the same way as Xilabu included the jarguci Alanzhu and the meiren ejen Na'ercha.

sentences.zh: 阿蘭珠，棟鄂氏，世居瓦爾喀什。

translations.literal: Alanzhu, of the Dong'o clan, had long resided at Warkashi.
translations.idiomatic: Alanzhu belonged to the Dong'o clan and came from a family long settled at Warkashi.

sentences.zh: 父阿格巴顏，與其兄對齊巴顏並為屯長。

translations.literal: His father Agebayan and his elder brother Duiqibayan were both village headmen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Agebayan and his uncle Duiqibayan both served as village headmen.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻杭佳城，守城者為阿格巴顏妻父，令助守，阿格巴顏不可，曰：「以德誅亂，宜也。

translations.literal: When Taizu attacked Hangjia Castle, the defender was Agebayan's wife's father. He ordered Agebayan to help hold the city, but Agebayan refused, saying: "To punish disorder with virtue is right.
translations.idiomatic: When Nurhaci attacked Hangjia Castle, the garrison commander was Agebayan's father-in-law, who ordered him to help defend the walls. Agebayan refused: "It is right to put down rebellion with virtue.

sentences.zh: 吾安能助亂而拒有德乎？」

translations.literal: How could I aid disorder and reject the virtuous?"
translations.idiomatic: How can I aid rebels and turn away a righteous cause?"

sentences.zh: 尋與對齊巴顏各率所屬歸太祖。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he and Duiqibayan each led their followers to submit to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Duiqibayan each led their people to join Nurhaci.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established, he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were organized, he was assigned to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 對齊巴顏子噶爾瑚濟、阿蘭珠皆授牛錄額真，分轄所屬。

translations.literal: Duiqibayan's sons Ga'erhuji and Alanzhu were both appointed niru ejen and divided authority over their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Duiqibayan's sons Ga'erhuji and Alanzhu were made niru commanders and given separate charge of their households.

sentences.zh: 阿蘭珠旋擢扎爾固齊。

translations.literal: Alanzhu was soon promoted to jarguci.
translations.idiomatic: Alanzhu was soon made jarguci.

sentences.zh: 從伐烏喇，直前衝擊，人馬皆被創，下馬步戰，遂沒於陣。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Ula he charged straight ahead; both man and horse were wounded. He dismounted to fight on foot and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the war against Ula he led the charge; man and horse were both wounded. He fought on foot and died in the line.

sentences.zh: 卹贈三等甲喇章京，以其弟布爾堪襲。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted third-rank jalan janggin, and his younger brother Bu'erkan succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made third-rank jalan janggin, and his younger brother Bu'erkan inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 順治間，追諡順毅。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi period he was posthumously titled Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi he was posthumously titled Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 布爾堪襲職，授甲喇額真。

translations.literal: Bu'erkan succeeded to the office and was appointed jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Bu'erkan inherited the post and was appointed jalan ejen.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，與武賴、哈寧阿等率精兵百略明邊，獲明諜三，遂渡大凌河，斬四十餘級，俘百六十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong, with Wulai, Haning'a, and others he led a hundred picked troops to raid the Ming frontier, captured three Ming spies, crossed the Daling River, beheaded more than forty, and took one hundred sixty captives.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4, with Wulai and Haning'a he led a hundred elite troops against the Ming border, took three spies, crossed the Daling River, killed more than forty, and captured one hundred sixty.

sentences.zh: 八年，重定各牛錄所屬人戶，以新附瑚爾哈百人增隸布爾堪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the households attached to each niru were reassigned, and one hundred newly submitted Hurha were added to Bu'erkan's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the niru household rolls were reorganized, and one hundred newly submitted Hurha were placed under Bu'erkan.

sentences.zh: 尋戍牛莊，獲蒙古逃人，進二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he garrisoned Niuzhuang, captured a Mongol fugitive, and was advanced to second-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He later garrisoned Niuzhuang, captured a Mongol deserter, and was promoted to second-rank jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chongde 1.

sentences.zh: 納爾察，鈕祜祿氏，世居安圖，隸蘇克蘇滸河部。

translations.literal: Na'ercha, of the Niohuru clan, had long resided at Antu and belonged to the Sukusuhu River division.
translations.idiomatic: Na'ercha of the Niohuru clan came from Antu in the Sukusuhu River group.

sentences.zh: 國初來歸，授備禦，隸滿洲鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he submitted and was granted the rank of beyde; he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he came over, received the rank of beyde, and was assigned to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 歲戊申，從太祖討烏喇，攻伊罕阿林城，先登克之，擢梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the year wushen he followed Taizu against Ula, attacked Yihan Alin Castle, was first to scale the walls and take it, and was promoted to meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In wushen he joined Nurhaci's campaign against Ula, was first over the wall at Yihan Alin Castle, and was made meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 後攻沙嶺，不待大軍至，獨進，沒於陣，以長子佛索里襲世職。

translations.literal: Later, attacking Shaling, he advanced alone before the main army arrived and died in battle; his eldest son Fosuoli succeeded to the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaling he pushed ahead before the main force arrived and fell in battle; his eldest son Fosuoli inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 順治間，追諡端壯。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi period he was posthumously titled Duanzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi he was posthumously titled Duanzhuang.

sentences.zh: 瑚沙，納爾察次子。

translations.literal: Husha was Na'ercha's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Husha was Na'ercha's second son.

sentences.zh: 初授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: He was first appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 天聰六年，從太宗伐明，入大同。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiancong he followed Taizong against the Ming and entered Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 6 he followed Hong Taiji's Ming campaign and entered Datong.

sentences.zh: 與圖魯什等行偵敵，遇明兵四百，瑚沙彎弓躍馬，疾馳入陣，敵皆披靡。

translations.literal: Scouting with Tulushi and others, he met four hundred Ming soldiers, strung his bow, spurred his horse, and charged straight into their ranks; the enemy broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: While scouting with Tulushi he met four hundred Ming troops, strung his bow, spurred straight into their ranks, and sent them flying.

sentences.zh: 略地至崞縣，屢擊敗明兵。

translations.literal: Raids reached as far as Guo County, repeatedly defeating Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: The columns pushed to Guo County and repeatedly routed Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，從貝勒岳託伐明，與鰲拜先驅，遇明騎兵三百，突出搏戰，瑚沙以八騎擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he followed Prince Yue Tuo against the Ming. With Oboi in the vanguard he met three hundred Ming cavalry, burst out to grapple with them, and Husha with eight horsemen drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 he joined Yueto's Ming campaign. With Oboi in the lead he met three hundred Ming horsemen; Husha with eight riders beat them back.

sentences.zh: 遂率左翼擺牙喇兵越燕京，徇山東。

translations.literal: He then led the Left Wing bayara troops past Yanjing and swept through Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He then led Left Wing bayara troops past Yanjing and through Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明太監高起潛等率兵出禦，瑚沙與羅什等連戰皆捷，逐北數十里。

translations.literal: When the Ming eunuch Gao Qiqian and others led troops out to oppose him, Husha with Roshi and others won successive victories and pursued them north for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Qiqian and other Ming eunuchs marched out, Husha and Roshi won a string of fights and chased them north for miles.

sentences.zh: 上以佛索里不勝任，畀瑚沙襲世職，為噶布什賢章京。

translations.literal: Because the khan judged Fosuoli unfit for the post, Husha was given the hereditary office and made a gūsa beise janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Fosuoli unfit, the khan transferred the hereditary rank to Husha and made him gūsa beise janggin.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐明，攻錦州，轉戰松山、杏山間，屢有斬獲。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the campaign against the Ming, attacked Jinzhou, and fought around Songshan and Xingshan, repeatedly taking heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the Ming campaign, fought at Jinzhou, and ranged between Songshan and Xingshan with repeated captures.

sentences.zh: 七年，加半個前程。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was granted half a step of salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he received half a step of salary.

sentences.zh: 十月，貝勒阿巴泰等帥師伐明，上命瑚沙從，俟師入邊，以軍事還報。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Prince Abatai and others commanded an army against the Ming. The khan ordered Husha to follow; once the army had crossed the border he was to return and report on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Abatai led an expedition against the Ming. The khan ordered Husha to accompany the force and, once it had crossed the border, to ride back with a military report.

sentences.zh: 八年春，師還，使瑚沙從噶布什賢噶喇昂邦努山等，以兵九。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, when the army returned, Husha was sent with the gūsa beise angbang Nushan and others with a force of ninety
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year, when the army returned, Husha was sent with Nushan, the gūsa beise angbang, and others at the head of ninety

translations.literal: ten
translations.idiomatic: ten

sentences.zh: 十人詣界嶺口迎師，俘敵甚

translations.literal: men to Jieling Pass to meet the army and took many enemy captives.
translations.idiomatic: men to Jieling Pass to welcome the returning army and captured a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關擊李自成，戰於一片石，瑚沙率本旗噶布什賢超哈當自成將唐通，逐自成至慶都；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the pass to strike Li Zicheng. At Yipianshi, Husha led his banner's gūsa beise cuha against Li's general Tang Tong, pursued Li Zicheng to Qingdu;
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shunzhi he crossed the pass to strike Li Zicheng. At Yipianshi, Husha led his banner's gūsa beise cuha against Tang Tong, Li's general, and chased Li Zicheng to Qingdu;

sentences.zh: 復從噶布什賢噶喇昂邦席特庫設謀誘敵，夾擊破之。

translations.literal: again, with the gūsa beise angbang Xitek, he laid a stratagem to lure the enemy and broke them in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: then, with Xitek, the gūsa beise angbang, he set a trap, drew the enemy in, and crushed them in a converging attack.

sentences.zh: 六月，從固山額真葉臣徵山西，至汾州，偕甲喇額真道喇、圖爾賽等，擊破自成將白輝。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he followed the gūsa ejen Yechen to campaign in Shanxi. Reaching Fenzhou, together with the jalan ejen Daola, Tuerse, and others, he defeated Li Zicheng's general Bai Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he marched into Shanxi under Yechen, reached Fenzhou, and with Daola, Tuerse, and others broke the force of Li's general Bai Hui.

sentences.zh: 二年，從英親王阿濟格徵陝西，克綏德、延安。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed the Prince Ying Ajige to campaign in Shaanxi and captured Suide and Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he followed Prince Ying Ajige into Shaanxi and took Suide and Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 牛錄額真哈爾漢俄班駐軍南山，為賊所乘，戰死，瑚沙率數騎突入，得其屍以還。

translations.literal: The niru ejen Harhan'eban garrisoned Nanshan and was caught by bandits and killed in battle. Husha led several horsemen in a sudden charge, recovered his body, and brought it back.
translations.idiomatic: When the niru commander Harhan'eban was caught on Nanshan and killed, Husha charged in with a handful of riders and brought his body back.

sentences.zh: 自成奔湖廣，追剿至安陸，擊敗自成將邵章，掠其舟以東。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng fled to Huguang. Pursuing him to Anlu, they defeated Li's general Shao Zhang and seized his boats to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng fled into Huguang. The pursuit reached Anlu, where they routed his general Shao Zhang and captured his boats downstream.

sentences.zh: 至九江口，與席特庫率前鋒二十人破賊壘，逐自成至於九宮山。

translations.literal: At Jiujiangkou, with Xitek he led twenty vanguard men, broke a bandit stronghold, and pursued Li Zicheng to Jiugong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiujiangkou he and Xitek led twenty vanguard fighters, stormed a rebel stockade, and chased Li Zicheng to Jiugong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 自成既殕，瑚沙復與甲喇額真蘇拜、希爾根等逐捕餘賊，斬二千餘級，進三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: After Li Zicheng had perished, Husha again, with the jalan ejen Subai, Xiergen, and others, hunted down the remaining bandits, beheaded more than two thousand, and was advanced to third-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Zicheng's death, Husha joined Subai, Xiergen, and others in mopping up the remnants, took more than two thousand heads, and was raised to third-rank jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 三年，從肅親王豪格討張獻忠於漢中，擊敗叛將賀迎戰，瑚沙奮擊敗之，肅親王遂殪獻忠。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong in Hanzhong. Defeating the rebel general He Zhen, who came out to offer battle, Husha fought fiercely and broke him, and Prince Su thereupon killed Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Suha against Zhang Xianzhong in Hanzhong. When the rebel He Zhen marched out to fight, Husha smashed his line, clearing the way for Suha to slay Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 五年，進二等阿達？

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to second-rank ada hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to second-rank ada hafan.

sentences.zh: 珍，逐獻忠至於西充，獻忠引哈哈番。

translations.literal: Pursuing Xianzhong's remnants to Xichong, he destroyed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued Zhang Xianzhong's remnants to Xichong and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 六年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗略湖南。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhala in raiding Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Prince Jirhala's sweep through Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時明桂王由榔猶駐廣西，其總督何騰蛟守湘潭。

translations.literal: At that time the Ming Prince of Gui, Youlang, was still in Guangxi, and his governor He Tengjiao held Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui, Youlang, still held Guangxi, and his governor He Tengjiao defended Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 師既克長沙，渡湘水攻之，前鋒兵薄城，敵分三門出戰，瑚沙與席特庫力戰，破城西兵，生致騰蛟。

translations.literal: Once the army had taken Changsha and crossed the Xiang River to attack, the vanguard pressed the city. The enemy came out through three gates to fight; Husha and Xitek fought hard, broke the western gate force, and captured Tengjiao alive.
translations.idiomatic: After Changsha fell the army crossed the Xiang and assaulted the city. When the defenders sallied from three gates, Husha and Xitek broke the western force and took Tengjiao alive.

sentences.zh: 明兵潰，遂克湘潭，於是衡州、寶慶、永州、辰州諸郡縣次第皆下。

translations.literal: The Ming army collapsed, Xiangtan fell, and thereafter Hengzhou, Baqing, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and other prefectures and counties were taken in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming line broke, Xiangtan fell, and Hengzhou, Baqing, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and the rest followed.

sentences.zh: 進二等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: He was advanced to second-rank ashan i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to second-rank ashan i hafan.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢鑲黃旗蒙古副都統，命與學士蘇納海使朝鮮鞫獄。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Mongol vice commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner and ordered, with Academician Sunahai, to go to Korea to investigate a legal case.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Mongol vice commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner and was sent with Academician Sunahai to try a case in Korea.

sentences.zh: 十一年，兼任工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he additionally served as vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he also served as vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢本旗蒙古都統，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Mongol commander of his banner and appointed a deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became Mongol commander of his banner and joined the Deliberative Council.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從信郡王多尼下雲南。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Prince Xin Duoni south into Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he followed Prince Xin Duoni's campaign into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十六年，從克永昌。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he followed in the capture of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he took part in the capture of Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 十七年，師還。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the army returned.

sentences.zh: 以永昌初下，縱兵入城擾民，降三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: Because when Yongchang was first taken he had allowed his troops to enter the city and harass the people, he was reduced to third-rank ashan i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongchang first fell he had let his men plunder the city; he was demoted to third-rank ashan i hafan.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 3.

sentences.zh: 分世職為二，第五子瑚弼圖襲一等阿達哈哈番，第二子碩伯海襲拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: The hereditary office was split in two: the fifth son Hubitu succeeded to first-rank ada hafan, and the second son Shuobohai succeeded to baitalabula hafan.
translations.idiomatic: The hereditary rank was divided: the fifth son Hubitu inherited first-rank ada hafan, and the second son Shuobohai inherited baitalabula hafan.

sentences.zh: =達音布=達音布，他塔喇氏，世居札庫木。

translations.literal: Dayinbu, of the Tatara clan, had long resided at Zhakumu.
translations.idiomatic: Dayinbu of the Tatara clan came from a family long settled at Zhakumu.

sentences.zh: 天命三年來歸，隸滿洲正白旗，任牛錄章京。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianming he submitted and was enrolled in the Manchu Plain White Banner as niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 3 he came over, joined the Manchu Plain White Banner, and served as niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 從太或為蒙古誘遁，達音布與楞額禮率兵逐之，？

translations.literal: When followers were lured away and fled to the Mongols, Dayinbu with Leng'e Li led troops in pursuit,
translations.idiomatic: When men were lured away and fled to the Mongols, Dayinbu and Leng'e Li pursued them,

sentences.zh: 祖征伐，輒為軍鋒，積戰閥授備禦。

translations.literal: and in Taizu's campaigns he always served in the vanguard; for accumulated battle merit he was granted the rank of beyde.
translations.idiomatic: and in Nurhaci's wars he always led the van; for repeated merit he received the rank of beyde.

sentences.zh: 來歸諸部及於達岱塔，擊敗蒙古兵，得逃人以歸。

translations.literal: When newly submitted tribes reached Dadatai, he routed Mongol detachments and recovered deserters.
translations.idiomatic: At Dadatai he beat back Mongol raiders and recovered fugitives from newly submitted groups.

sentences.zh: 六年，太祖伐明，略奉集堡，達音布先驅，斬諜克敵，進游擊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Taizu attacked the Ming and raided Fengji Fort, Dayinbu rode in the vanguard, beheaded spies and overcame the enemy, and was advanced to guerrilla commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, during Nurhaci's raid on Fengji Fort, Dayinbu led the van, killed enemy scouts, and was made guerrilla commandant.

sentences.zh: 蒙古扎魯特貝勒昂安嘗執我使畀葉赫，又屢遣兵要我使，攘牲畜。

translations.literal: The Mongol Zhalute beile Ang'an had once seized our envoy and handed him to Yehe, and repeatedly sent troops to intercept our envoys and seize livestock.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhalute beile Ang'an had seized a Qing envoy and sent him to Yehe, and repeatedly waylaid envoys and drove off livestock.

sentences.zh: 八年，太祖命台吉阿巴泰等將三千人討之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Taizu ordered the taiji Abatai and others to lead three thousand men against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Nurhaci sent the taiji Abatai with three thousand men against him.

sentences.zh: 達音佈時為噶布什賢噶喇昂邦，與雅希禪、博爾晉率五十騎先大軍行，乘夜渡遼河，略昂安所轄厄爾格勒，复馳百餘裡，逼昂安所居寨，昂安以牛車載妻子率從者二十餘騎出寨。

translations.literal: Dayinbu, then gūsa beise angbang, with Yaxican and Bo'erjin led fifty horsemen ahead of the main army, crossed the Liao River by night, raided Ang'an's district of Ergele, then galloped more than a hundred li and pressed Ang'an's stockade. Ang'an loaded his wife and children onto ox carts and came out of the stockade with a little more than twenty followers on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Dayinbu, then gūsa beise angbang, with Yaxican and Bo'erjin took fifty horsemen ahead of the army, crossed the Liao by night, raided Ergele, and rode more than a hundred li to Ang'an's camp. Ang'an put wife and children in ox carts and came out with some twenty riders.

sentences.zh: 雅希禪、博爾晉麾三十餘騎下馬將搏戰，達音布引十餘騎勒馬立，昂安謀遁，不欲戰，直前衝騎兵，冀突圍出，達音布拒戰，方彎弓注矢，昂安所部乘隙挾短矛？

translations.literal: Yaxican and Bo'erjin dismounted with a little more than thirty horsemen to grapple; Dayinbu held ten-odd horsemen in check at the rein. Ang'an planned to flee and did not wish to fight, but charged straight at the cavalry hoping to break out. Dayinbu blocked him; as he was bending the bow to nock an arrow, Ang'an's men seized the opening and thrust short spears at Dayinbu,
translations.idiomatic: Yaxican and Bo'erjin dismounted with thirty riders to fight; Dayinbu held a dozen horsemen in reserve. Ang'an meant to flee, then charged the line to break out. As Dayinbu drew his bow, Ang'an's men thrust short spears at him,

sentences.zh: 達音布，中其口，墮馬。

translations.literal: striking Dayinbu in the mouth; he fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: wounding Dayinbu in the mouth and knocking him from his horse.

sentences.zh: 我兵衝擊，昂安父子及從者盡殪，俘其孥。

translations.literal: Our troops charged; Ang'an, his son, and all their followers were killed, and their families were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing line surged forward; Ang'an, his son, and their followers were all killed and their families taken.

sentences.zh: 達音布遂以創卒。

translations.literal: Dayinbu then died of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Dayinbu died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 師還，予卹，進世​​職為游擊。

translations.literal: When the army returned, posthumous grants were made and the hereditary office was advanced to guerrilla commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he received posthumous honors and the hereditary rank was raised to guerrilla commandant.

sentences.zh: 崇？

translations.literal: Chongde
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongde period,

sentences.zh: 子阿濟格尼堪，阿濟格尼堪子宜理布，並有傳。

translations.literal: His son Ajigenikan and Ajigenikan's son Yilibu each have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ajigenikan and Ajigenikan's son Yilibu are each given separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 第三子岱袞，屢從征伐，授侍德二年，圍錦州，戰死，贈備禦。

translations.literal: His third son Daigun repeatedly followed campaigns and received a hereditary office. In the second year of Chongde, besieging Jinzhou, he died in battle and was posthumously granted beyde.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Daigun fought in many campaigns and held a hereditary rank. In Chongde 2, while besieging Jinzhou, he fell in battle and was posthumously made beyde.

sentences.zh: 達音布死最烈，子孫貴列爵，順治間賜諡乃不及。

translations.literal: Dayinbu died most heroically, yet though his descendants rose to noble ranks, in the Shunzhi period no posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Dayinbu's death was the most valiant, yet although his line rose to noble rank, Shunzhi never granted him a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 太祖諸偏裨死事者，牛錄額真喀喇，以御劉綎戰死。

translations.literal: Among Taizu's junior officers who died in service, the niru ejen Kala died fighting Liu Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Among Nurhaci's company officers who died in service, the niru ejen Kala fell fighting Liu Ting.

sentences.zh: 又有牛錄額真額爾納、額黑乙，將五百人屯深河，與綎戰林中，死之。

translations.literal: There were also the niru ejen E'erna and Eheyi, who with five hundred men garrisoned Shenhe, fought Liu Ting in the forest, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The niru ejen E'erna and Eheyi also garrisoned Shenhe with five hundred men, fought Liu Ting in the woods, and died.

sentences.zh: 甲喇額真布哈、石爾泰，牛錄額真朗格，從太祖攻瀋陽，既下，明總兵陳策等來援，與戰，陷陣死。

translations.literal: The jalan ejen Buha and Shi'ertai, and the niru ejen Langge, followed Taizu in attacking Shenyang. After it fell, Ming regional commander Chen Ce and others came to relieve the city. They joined battle and died in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: The jalan ejen Buha and Shi'ertai and the niru ejen Langge followed the attack on Shenyang. When Chen Ce and other Ming generals came to relieve the city, all three died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾當圖從太祖圍錦州，戰死。

translations.literal: Ma'erdangtu followed Taizu in besieging Jinzhou and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ma'erdangtu died besieging Jinzhou under Nurhaci.

sentences.zh: 喀喇、額爾納、額黑乙死時，太祖方草創，未有卹贈。

translations.literal: When Kala, E'erna, and Eheyi died, Taizu was still in the founding stage and had not yet established posthumous grants.
translations.idiomatic: When Kala, E'erna, and Eheyi fell, the dynasty was still being founded and no posthumous honors yet existed.

sentences.zh: 布哈贈參將，石爾泰、朗格贈游擊，而瑪爾當圖死時已授游擊。

translations.literal: Buha was posthumously granted regimental commander; Shi'ertai and Langge were posthumously granted guerrilla commandant, while Ma'erdangtu had already held guerrilla commandant when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Buha was posthumously made regimental commander; Shi'ertai and Langge received guerrilla commandant; Ma'erdangtu already held that rank when he died.

sentences.zh: 朗格子和託、瑪爾當圖子烏庫理事太宗，喀喇孫舒裡渾、洛多歡、崆古圖事世祖，皆有戰功，賞延於世。

translations.literal: Langge's son Hetuo and Ma'erdangtu's son Wukuli served Taizong; Kala's grandsons Shulihun, Luoduo, and Kuangutu served Shizu—all had battle merit, and rewards extended to their heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Langge's son Hetuo and Ma'erdangtu's son Wukuli served Hong Taiji; Kala's grandsons Shulihun, Luoduo, and Kuangutu served Shunzhi—all won distinction, and their honors passed down the line.

sentences.zh: 朗格，棟鄂氏，對齊巴顏子，阿蘭珠弟也。

translations.literal: Langge, of the Dong'o clan, was Duiqibayan's son and Alanzhu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Langge of the Dong'o clan was Duiqibayan's son and Alanzhu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 對齊巴顏來歸，語見阿蘭珠傳。

translations.literal: Duiqibayan's submission is recounted in Alanzhu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Duiqibayan's coming over is told in Alanzhu's biography.

sentences.zh: 戰死，得世職，以長子棟世祿襲。

translations.literal: He died in battle and received a hereditary office, which his eldest son Dongshilu succeeded to.
translations.idiomatic: He died in battle and left a hereditary rank that passed to his eldest son Dongshilu.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established, he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the banners were organized, the family was assigned to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 和託，其次子也。

translations.literal: Hetuo was his second son.
translations.idiomatic: Hetuo was Langge's second son.

sentences.zh: 崇德七年正月，授本旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Chongde he was appointed meiren ejen of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongde 7 he was made meiren ejen of his banner.

sentences.zh: 從鄭親王濟爾哈朗等伐明，圍錦州。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Zheng Jirhala and others against the Ming and besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Prince Jirhala's campaign against the Ming and helped besiege Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 明總兵祖大壽以其城降，遂進克塔山。

translations.literal: Ming regional commander Zu Dashou surrendered the city, and the army then advanced and took Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Dashou surrendered Jinzhou, the army pushed on and took Tashan.

sentences.zh: 鄭親王籍所俘獲，令和託還奏。

translations.literal: Prince Zheng registered the booty captured and ordered Hetuo to return and report.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jirhala tallied the spoils and sent Hetuo back to court with the report.

sentences.zh: 上命分賚軍中死傷將士，並令齎敕撫明杏山守將，曰：「汝以善言招之，降則已；

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered rewards distributed to wounded and slain officers and soldiers in the army, and also ordered him to carry an edict to conciliate the Ming garrison commander at Xingshan, saying: 'You are to win him with fair words; if he submits, that is enough;
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Hetuo to distribute rewards among the army's wounded and dead and to carry an edict to the Ming commander at Xingshan: 'Win him with fair words; if he yields, so be it;

sentences.zh: 否則以砲攻，砲發而彼降，亦可許也。」

translations.literal: otherwise attack with cannon; if he submits after the cannon fire, that too may be accepted.'
translations.idiomatic: otherwise bombard the place—and if he submits after the guns open fire, accept that as well.'

sentences.zh: 和託至軍，如上指宣示，砲發，明將降。

translations.literal: Hetuo reached the army, announced this as instructed; the cannon fired, and the Ming commander submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hetuo reached the front, delivered the orders, opened fire, and the Ming commander surrendered.

sentences.zh: 師還，得優賚。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he received special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was handsomely rewarded.

sentences.zh: 旋追議諸將徇部卒失律，和託當罰鍰，以前勞得免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, when generals who had indulged their troops' breaches of discipline were reviewed for punishment, Hetuo was liable to a fine but was exempted on account of earlier merit.
translations.idiomatic: When commanders who had let their men break discipline were later called to account, Hetuo should have paid a fine, but past service won him a reprieve.

sentences.zh: 十月，從貝勒阿巴泰伐明，自界嶺口毀邊牆入，至黃崖口。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he followed Beile Abatai against the Ming, broke through the border wall at Jieling Pass, and advanced to Huangyakou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he joined Beile Abatai's raid into Ming territory, smashed the border wall at Jieling Pass, and pushed on to Huangyakou.

sentences.zh: 軍中議分兩翼夾攻，輔國公斐洋古令和託督左翼，建雲梯攻城。

translations.literal: The army debated a two-wing pincer attack; Prince Fu Feiyanggu ordered Hetuo to command the left wing and erect scaling ladders for the assault.
translations.idiomatic: The command planned a pincer attack; Prince Fu Feiyanggu put Hetuo in charge of the left wing and ordered scaling ladders built for the assault.

sentences.zh: 和託週視畢，復曰：「城可登，無以梯為也。」

translations.literal: After Hetuo had made a full circuit of inspection, he said again: 'The wall can be climbed; there is no need for ladders.'
translations.idiomatic: After riding all the way around the defenses, Hetuo said, 'The wall can be taken without ladders.'

sentences.zh: 乃率巴牙喇兵四十人毀城入，斬守備一，餘悉潰。

translations.literal: He then led forty bayara troops, broke through the wall and entered, beheaded one garrison commandant, and the rest all fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then took forty bayara troops through a breach in the wall, killed a garrison commandant, and routed the rest.

sentences.zh: 復合右翼圍薊州，擊敗明總兵白騰蛟、白廣恩，遂徇山東，克兗、萊、青諸府。

translations.literal: Rejoining the right wing, he besieged Jizhou, defeated Ming regional commanders Bai Tengjiao and Bai Guang'en, and then marched through Shandong, taking the prefectures of Yan, Lai, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoined the right wing to invest Jizhou, routed the Ming generals Bai Tengjiao and Bai Guang'en, then swept through Shandong and captured Yanzhou, Laizhou, and Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，師還，授吏部參政、兼梅勒額真。

translations.literal: The next year, when the army returned, he was appointed minister of the Board of Civil Appointments and concurrently meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on the army's return, he was made a minister of the Board of Civil Appointments and retained his post as meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關擊李自成，予世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the Pass to strike Li Zicheng and was granted the hereditary office of niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he crossed into China with the army against Li Zicheng and received the hereditary rank of niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎王鰲永招撫山東，明副總兵楊威據登州。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Vice Minister Wang Aoyong to win over Shandong; Ming vice regional commander Yang Wei held Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent Vice Minister Wang Aoyong to pacify Shandong, while the Ming vice commander Yang Wei held Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 鰲永請兵，上命和託與梅勒額真李率泰、額孟格帥師討之。

translations.literal: Aoyong requested troops; the Emperor ordered Hetuo, together with meiren ejen Li Shuaitai and Emuge, to lead an army against him.
translations.idiomatic: Aoyong asked for reinforcements, and the court ordered Hetuo, Li Shuaitai, and Emuge to march against Yang Wei.

sentences.zh: 鰲永至青州，為降將趙應元所戕。

translations.literal: When Aoyong reached Qingzhou, he was murdered by the surrendered general Zhao Yingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Aoyong reached Qingzhou only to be killed by the turncoat Zhao Yingyuan.

sentences.zh: 和託等師至，牒巡撫陳錦、總兵柯永盛會師逼青州。

translations.literal: When Hetuo's army arrived, he sent dispatches to Governor Chen Jin and regional commander Ke Yongsheng to join forces and press Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hetuo's force arrived and summoned Governor Chen Jin and Commander Ke Yongsheng to combine and close on Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 應元復請降，和託與李率泰計許之降，遣兵夜捕斬應元及其黨數十人，宥脅從勿誅，青州遂定。

translations.literal: Yingyuan again asked to submit; Hetuo and Li Shuaitai planned to pretend to accept his surrender, sent troops by night to seize and behead Yingyuan and several dozen of his followers, spared those coerced into joining, and Qingzhou was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan offered to surrender again; Hetuo and Li Shuaitai feigned acceptance, then sent men by night to capture and execute him and dozens of his partisans, pardoned the compelled followers, and Qingzhou was secured.

sentences.zh: 錦亦下登州。

translations.literal: Chen Jin also took Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jin took Dengzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 上命和託與李率泰移軍河南，會豫親王多鐸下江南，賚黃金、紫貂，進世職三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Hetuo and Li Shuaitai to move the army to Henan, join Prince Yu Dodo's descent into Jiangnan, granted them gold and sable, and promoted his hereditary office to third-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Hetuo and Li Shuaitai were ordered into Henan to link up with Prince Dodo's drive into the south; they received gold and sable furs, and Hetuo's hereditary rank rose to third-class jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 二年，從貝勒勒克德渾徇浙江，定杭州。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Beile Lekdehun in a sweep of Zhejiang and settled Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he joined Beile Lekdehun's campaign through Zhejiang and helped secure Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明將方國安以兵至，和託將左翼御之富陽，斬副將二、參將二、游擊五，國安兵大敗。

translations.literal: When the Ming general Fang Guo'an came with troops, Hetuo commanded the left wing to meet him at Fuyang, beheaded two vice commanders, two regimental commanders, and five guerrilla commanders, and Fang Guo'an's army was heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Guo'an advanced with his army, Hetuo took the left wing at Fuyang, killed two vice commanders, two regimental commanders, and five guerrilla commanders, and routed Fang's force completely.

sentences.zh: 复破敵下關直溝，毀其木城。

translations.literal: He again broke the enemy at Xiaguan Zhigou and destroyed their wooden fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the enemy again at Xiaguan Zhigou and tore down their timber palisade.

sentences.zh: 上命和託與梅勒額真珠瑪喇率所部滿洲、蒙古兵駐防杭州。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Hetuo and meiren ejen Jumala to lead their Manchu and Mongol troops to garrison Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hetuo and Jumala were ordered to station their Manchu and Mongol troops at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Shunzhi 3.

sentences.zh: 雍舜，對齊巴顏從子，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Yongshun was Duiqibayan's younger clansman's son and was appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshun, a younger kinsman of Duiqibayan, held the post of niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 英果，戰輒當前鋒。

translations.literal: Bold and resolute, in battle he always took the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Fearless in combat, he invariably led the van.

sentences.zh: 累擢鑲紅旗固山額真。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to gusai ejen of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to become gusai ejen of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從上伐明，圍遵化，率本旗兵攻城西南，克之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he followed the Emperor against the Ming, besieged Zunhua, led his banner's troops against the southwest of the city, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 he joined the campaign against the Ming, besieged Zunhua, and led his banner's men in storming the southwest corner of the city.

sentences.zh: 四年，從取永平，授二等參將世職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the capture of Yongping and was granted a second-rank regimental commander's hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4 he helped take Yongping and received a hereditary second-rank regimental commander's rank.

sentences.zh: 貝勒阿敏棄永平還師，雍舜獨贊其議，坐罷官，奪世職，籍沒。

translations.literal: When Beile Amin abandoned Yongping and withdrew, Yongshun alone approved that decision; he was dismissed from office, stripped of his hereditary office, and his property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When Beile Amin abandoned Yongping and pulled back, Yongshun alone defended the decision; he was removed from office, stripped of his hereditary rank, and his estate was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 七年，從貝勒岳託舟師攻旅順，明將黃龍城守，師克之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Beile Yoto's fleet against Lüshun; Ming general Huang Long defended the city, and the army took it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 7 he joined Beile Yoto's naval assault on Lüshun; though Huang Long held the city, the fleet carried it.

sentences.zh: 論功，先登崖者，巴奇蘭、薩穆什喀；

translations.literal: When merit was assessed, those who first scaled the cliff were Baqilan and Samushka;
translations.idiomatic: In the reckoning of honors, Baqilan and Samushka were credited with first scaling the bluff;

sentences.zh: 先登城者，雍舜、珠瑪喇：复世職。

translations.literal: those who first scaled the wall were Yongshun and Jumala: their hereditary offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: while Yongshun and Jumala were credited with first mounting the wall—and their hereditary ranks were restored.

sentences.zh: 崇德二年，從克皮島，擢梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongde he followed the capture of Pi Island and was promoted to meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 2 he joined the capture of Pi Island and was made meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 四年，從征索倫，設伏敗敵，進一等參將。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed a campaign against the Solon, set an ambush and defeated the enemy, and was promoted to first-rank regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 4 he campaigned against the Solon, ambushed and routed the enemy, and rose to first-rank regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，從攻錦州，戰墜馬，得他騎，引本旗兵趨左翼；

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the attack on Jinzhou, fell from his horse in battle, obtained another mount, and led his banner's troops toward the left wing;
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 6, assaulting Jinzhou, he was unhorsed, seized another mount, and led his banner toward the left wing;

sentences.zh: 及右翼勝，乃馳擊，爭赴敵。

translations.literal: when the right wing had won, he then galloped to the attack and vied to reach the enemy first.
translations.idiomatic: and once the right wing prevailed, he charged in and raced his men to meet the foe.

sentences.zh: 坐欺謾論罪，命寬之，解梅勒額真。

translations.literal: He was judged guilty of deceit and condemned, but the sentence was lenient and he was removed as meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of deceit, he was spared the harshest penalty but lost his post as meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 順治初，遇恩詔，進二等阿思哈尼哈番，复官固山額真。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, on an amnesty edict, he was promoted to second-rank ashan i hafan and restored as gusai ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi an amnesty raised him to second-rank ashan i hafan and restored him as gusai ejen.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子庚圖，先以功授拜他喇布勒哈番，同為一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: His son Gengtu had earlier been granted baitalabure hafan for merit and likewise became first-rank ashan i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gengtu, already a baitalabure hafan for earlier service, eventually held first-rank ashan i hafan as well.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾當圖，扎庫塔氏，先世居和克通吉。

translations.literal: Ma'erdangtu, of the Zakuta clan, had ancestors who long resided at Heketongji.
translations.idiomatic: Ma'erdangtu of the Zakuta clan came from a family long settled at Heketongji.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，率百餘人，授游擊。

translations.literal: In the time of the Taizu, he led a little over a hundred men and was appointed guerrilla commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taizu he led a little more than a hundred men and received the rank of guerrilla commandant.

sentences.zh: 從攻錦州，戰死。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Jinzhou and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Jinzhou and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子烏庫理，年十六，即從征伐。

translations.literal: His son Wukuli, at the age of sixteen, already followed campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wukuli took the field at sixteen.

sentences.zh: 太宗命領甲喇額真，襲瑪爾當圖世職。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered him to lead as jalan ejen and to succeed to Ma'erdangtu's hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji made him jalan ejen and heir to Ma'erdangtu's hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，從貝勒岳託伐明，略山東，明太監馮永盛以兵至，擊敗之；

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he followed Beile Yoto against the Ming and swept Shandong; when Ming eunuch Feng Yongsheng came with troops, Wukuli defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 he joined Beile Yoto's raid into Shandong; when the Ming eunuch Feng Yongsheng marched out, Wukuli routed him;

sentences.zh: 攻濟南，雲梯兵未至，烏庫理攀雉堞先登，麾所部兵畢上，克其城。

translations.literal: in the attack on Jinan, before the scaling-ladder troops arrived, Wukuli climbed the battlements first, waved his troops up after him, and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: at Jinan, before the ladder corps arrived, he scaled the parapet first, brought his men up after him, and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 師還，將出塞，與白奇超哈統將薩穆什喀殿，敵不敢逼，道經太平寨，复步戰敗敵。

translations.literal: When the army returned and was about to leave the frontier, he and Baiqi Chaha commander Samushka formed the rearguard; the enemy did not dare press them, and on the road at Taipingzhai he again defeated the enemy in foot combat.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he and Samushka covered the rear; the enemy dared not close, and at Taipingzhai he beat them again in a running fight.

sentences.zh: 七年，從伐明，復攻錦州，戰於松山，敵敗走，旋合潰兵屯北山，壘甚固，烏庫理直前擊之，三戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed a campaign against the Ming and again attacked Jinzhou; at Songshan the enemy fled, then rallied scattered troops and encamped on North Mountain with very strong fortifications; Wukuli pressed straight forward and attacked, and three battles were all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 7, back at Jinzhou and Songshan, he drove off the foe, then smashed their regrouped camp on North Mountain in three straight victories.

sentences.zh: 順治初，入關，從固山額真葉臣攻太原，率十騎繞城周視，城兵驟出搏戰，烏庫理與。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, after entering the Pass, he followed gusai ejen Yechen in attacking Taiyuan, led ten horsemen to ride around inspecting the wall, and when garrison troops suddenly sallied out to fight, Wukuli together with
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he entered the Pass with Yechen's assault on Taiyuan. Riding round the walls with ten horsemen, he was caught in a sudden sally; Wukuli and jalan ejen Sabitu fought back fiercely.

sentences.zh: 尋從英親王阿濟格定陝西、湖廣、江西諸省。

translations.literal: he then followed Prince Ying Ajige in settling Shaanxi, Huguang, and the provinces of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Prince Ajige in pacifying Shaanxi, Huguang, and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 師還，至池？

translations.literal: When the army returned, it reached Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march the army reached Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲喇額真薩璧圖奮擊，俘馘甚州，偵明將黃斐，擊之，得舟十二。

translations.literal: Jalan ejen Sabitu fought fiercely, killed and captured a great many; scouting Ming general Huang Fei, he attacked him and obtained twelve boats.
translations.idiomatic: They killed or captured a great many. Scouting the Ming officer Huang Fei, he attacked and seized twelve boats.

sentences.zh: 還京師，授兵部理事官，加半個前程。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was appointed a minister of the Board of War and granted half a step of seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he was made a minister of the Board of War and given half a step of promotion.

sentences.zh: 三年，從肅親王豪格下四川，討張獻忠，敗其將高汝礪；

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Su Hooge into Sichuan to suppress Zhang Xianzhong and defeated his general Gao Rulü;
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he joined Prince Hooge's descent into Sichuan against Zhang Xianzhong and defeated Gao Rulü;

sentences.zh: 逐獻忠，再破之。

translations.literal: pursuing Xianzhong, he defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: pursuing Xianzhong, he routed him a second time.

sentences.zh: 五年，從討叛將薑瓖，攻寧武關，所署巡撫姜輝、總兵劉惟思以三千人赴援，內外兵夾擊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed the suppression of the rebel Jiang Xiang, attacked Ningwu Pass; the appointed governor Jiang Hui and regional commander Liu Weisi came with three thousand men to relieve it, and inner and outer forces attacked together.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 he joined the campaign against Jiang Xiang and assaulted Ningwu Pass; Jiang Hui and Liu Weisi marched out with three thousand relief troops, and the besiegers and defenders struck from both sides.

sentences.zh: 烏庫理率三旗巴牙喇兵轉戰關下，瓖兵萬餘陣以待，烏庫理擊破之，復發砲克其城？

translations.literal: Wukuli led bayara troops of three banners fighting below the pass; Jiang's troops, more than ten thousand, drew up in battle order; Wukuli broke them and again opened fire with cannon and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wukuli led bayara from three banners in fighting below the pass; when Jiang's ten-thousand-man force formed for battle, Wukuli shattered them and blasted the city open with cannon.

sentences.zh: 及偏關西河營，七戰皆勝。

translations.literal: At Pianguan and the Xihe Camp as well, seven battles were all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: At Pianguan and the Xihe Camp too he won seven battles without defeat.

sentences.zh: 師將至左，殪瓖兵。

translations.literal: As the army was about to reach Zuoyun, Jiang Xiang's troops were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: As the army approached Zuoyun, Jiang Xiang's troops were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 八年，進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to first-rank adaha hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 he rose to first-rank adaha hafan.

sentences.zh: 十年，鄭成功寇福建，命與理事官額赫理率禁旅及江？

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when Zheng Chenggong raided Fujian, he was ordered, together with minister Eheli, to lead the imperial guard and the garrison troops of Jiangning
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10, when Zheng Chenggong threatened Fujian, he and Eheli were ordered to lead the imperial guard and the Jiangning

sentences.zh: 寧、杭州駐防兵濟師，至海澄，敵以火器守隘，烏庫理連破其壘。

translations.literal: and Hangzhou to reinforce the army; reaching Haicheng, the enemy held the passes with firearms, and Wukuli repeatedly broke their fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: and Hangzhou garrisons to the coast; at Haicheng the enemy blocked the defiles with gunfire, and Wukuli stormed fort after fort.

sentences.zh: 敵毀橋，烏庫理躍馬先涉，敵驚潰，師乃畢渡；

translations.literal: The enemy destroyed the bridge; Wukuli spurred his horse and crossed first; the enemy fled in alarm, and the army was then able to cross entirely;
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy broke the bridge, Wukuli was first across on horseback; they broke and ran, and the whole army got over;

sentences.zh: 敵又以三千餘人屯海岸，烏庫理步戰敗之。

translations.literal: the enemy again encamped more than three thousand men on the shore; Wukuli defeated them in foot combat.
translations.idiomatic: then three thousand more held the shore, and he beat them in a foot fight.

sentences.zh: 先後與固山額真金礪等，劘敵寨數十，降其兵數千人，復加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Successively, with gusai ejen Jin Li and others, he reduced several dozen enemy stockades, accepted the surrender of several thousand troops, and was again granted tooshan hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Working with Jin Li and others, he reduced dozens of enemy forts, accepted thousands of surrenders, and was again granted tooshan hafan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授大理寺卿，疏言：「滿洲士卒歲從征討，市馬制械皆自具，其孥留京師，請恩賚。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review and memorialized: 'Manchu soldiers year after year follow campaigns; they buy horses and make weapons at their own expense, while their wives and children remain in the capital—please grant them favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12 he became president of the Court of Judicial Review and submitted a memorial: Manchu troops campaigning year after year paid for their own horses and arms while their families stayed in the capital—he asked that they be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 行軍所至，民多失所，雖被旨賑貸，當安輯，俾自為生計，請？

translations.literal: Wherever the army marched, the people often lost their homes; although imperial orders granted relief, they should be settled and enabled to make their own livelihood—please have
translations.idiomatic: Wherever armies passed, people were often uprooted; though relief was ordered, they needed settlement and a way to live—he asked that

sentences.zh: 部議便宜。

translations.literal: the ministries discuss expedient measures.
translations.idiomatic: the ministries weigh practical measures.

sentences.zh: 綠旗死事將卒，請下所司贍其妻子。

translations.literal: For Green Banner officers and soldiers who died in service, he asked that orders be sent to the responsible offices to support their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: For Green Banner men fallen in service, he asked that the proper offices be ordered to provide for their families.

sentences.zh: 江、廣、閩、浙濱江、海，盜賊出沒，請敕諸省督撫，要隘設重兵。

translations.literal: Along the rivers and seas of Jiang, Guang, Min, and Zhe, bandits came and went; he asked that the governors-general of the provinces be instructed to station strong forces at key passes.
translations.idiomatic: On the coasts and rivers of Jiangsu, Guangdong, Fujian, and Zhejiang, bandits roamed; he urged heavy garrisons at critical points under provincial supervision.

sentences.zh: 西北厄魯特、俄羅斯諸部尚阻聲教，請敕理籓院議互市條例，通貿易。」
