translations.literal: In the northwest the Oirat, Russian, and other tribes still stood apart from civilization; he asked that the Court of Colonial Affairs be instructed to discuss trade regulations and open commerce.'
translations.idiomatic: In the northwest the Oirats, Russians, and other peoples still lay outside regular contact; he asked the Court of Colonial Affairs to frame trade rules and open exchange.

sentences.zh: 所陳凡五事，皆下部議行。

translations.literal: Of the five matters he presented, all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and action.
translations.idiomatic: All five proposals were sent to the ministries for review and implementation.

sentences.zh: 尋命視黃河決口。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to inspect the Yellow River breach.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to inspect a breach in the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed director-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 he became director-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授盛京總管。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed superintendent of Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 he was made superintendent of Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，改總管為將軍，仍以命烏庫理。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi the superintendent's post was changed to general, and Wukuli was again appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 the superintendency became a generalship, and Wukuli kept the command.

sentences.zh: 是時，盛京置戶、禮、工三部，烏庫理請增設刑部，廷議如所請。

translations.literal: At that time Shengjing had boards of Revenue, Rites, and Works; Wukuli requested that a Board of Punishments also be established, and the court deliberated and approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: Shengjing then had boards of Revenue, Rites, and Works; Wukuli asked that Punishments be added, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 4.

sentences.zh: 析世職為二，長子俄謨克圖，襲三等阿達哈哈番；

translations.literal: The hereditary office was divided in two: the eldest son Emuketu succeeded to third-rank adaha hafan;
translations.idiomatic: His hereditary honors were split: the eldest son Emuketu took third-rank adaha hafan;

sentences.zh: 次子佛保，襲拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: the second son Fobao succeeded to baitalabure hafan together with tooshan hafan.
translations.idiomatic: the second son Fobao to baitalabure hafan with tooshan hafan.

sentences.zh: 喀喇，棟鄂氏，先世居瓦爾喀。

translations.literal: Kala, of the Dong'o clan, had ancestors who long resided in Walha.
translations.idiomatic: Kala of the Dong'o clan came from a family long settled in Walha.

sentences.zh: 當太祖時，以其族來歸。

translations.literal: In the time of the Taizu, he came over with his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taizu his clan submitted.

sentences.zh: 從征伐有功，授牛錄額真，賜號「巴圖魯」。

translations.literal: He had merit in following campaigns and was appointed niru ejen and granted the title 'Baturu.'
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning brought him distinction; he became niru ejen and was named Baturu.

sentences.zh: 天命四年，禦明總兵劉綎，力戰，被七創，以傷卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianming he met Ming regional commander Liu Ting and fought fiercely, suffering seven wounds, and died of his injuries.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 4 he faced Liu Ting's Ming force, fought until he took seven wounds, and died of them.

sentences.zh: 子扎福尼。

translations.literal: His son Zhafuni.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhafuni.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，從伐明，攻灤州，有三卒為敵所得，扎福尼陷陣援之出。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong he followed a campaign against the Ming and attacked Luanzhou; three soldiers were taken by the enemy, and Zhafuni broke into the enemy ranks and rescued them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4, campaigning against the Ming at Luanzhou, he plunged into the enemy line to rescue three men captured by the foe.

sentences.zh: 以功，予世職備禦。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the hereditary office of beyu.
translations.idiomatic: For this he received the hereditary rank of beyu.

sentences.zh: 八年十二月，從白奇超哈統將巴奇蘭等伐黑龍江，加半個前程。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighth year he followed Baiqi Chaha commander Baqilan and others against the Amur and was granted half a step of seniority.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tiancong 8 he joined Baqilan's expedition on the Amur and gained half a step of promotion.

sentences.zh: 舒裡渾，扎福尼子也。

translations.literal: Shulihun was Zhafuni's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shulihun was Zhafuni's son.

sentences.zh: 初以巴牙喇壯達從軍。

translations.literal: At first he followed the army as a bayara da.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a bayara da.

sentences.zh: 從攻大凌河城，敗蒙古軍。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Dalinghe City and defeated the Mongol army.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Dalinghe and routed the Mongol force.

sentences.zh: 及扎福尼卒，襲世職。

translations.literal: When Zhafuni died, he succeeded to the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhafuni's death he inherited the family rank.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，從英親王阿濟格西逐李自成至延安，七捷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Ying Ajige west in pursuing Li Zicheng to Yan'an and won seven victories.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he followed Prince Ajige west in the pursuit of Li Zicheng to Yan'an and won seven engagements.

sentences.zh: 自成走湖廣，以師從之，次安陸，得舟十四。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled to Huguang; Shulihun followed with the army, halted at Anlu, and obtained fourteen boats.
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng fled into Huguang, Shulihun followed, halted at Anlu, and seized fourteen boats.

sentences.zh: 三年，從豫親王多鐸北討騰吉斯，力戰，多俘馘，擊敗喀爾喀土謝圖汗、碩類汗。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Yu Dodo north to suppress Tengjisi, fought fiercely, captured and killed many, and defeated the Khalkha Tüsiyetü Khan and Sholoi Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he joined Prince Dodo's northern campaign against Tengjisi, fought hard, took many heads and prisoners, and defeated the Khalkha Tüsiyetü and Sholoi khans.

sentences.zh: 師還，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 六年，從端重親王博洛西徇大同，擊敗姜瓖所署巡撫姜建勳等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo west in a sweep of Datong and defeated Jiang Xiang's appointed governor Jiang Jianxun and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he joined Prince Bolo's western sweep toward Datong and defeated Jiang Jianxun and other officers of Jiang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢巴牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to bayara tuwakibure janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 he was made bayara tuwakibure janggin.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授正黃旗滿洲梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed meiren ejen of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 he was made meiren ejen of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 從信郡王多尼南征雲南，戰涼水井，敗明將李成蛟；

translations.literal: He followed Prince Xin Duoni south in the campaign against Yunnan, fought at Liangshuijing, and defeated the Ming general Li Chengjiao;
translations.idiomatic: He joined Prince Duoni's southern expedition into Yunnan, fought at Liangshuijing, and routed the Ming commander Li Chengjiao;

sentences.zh: 戰雙河口，敗明將李定國。

translations.literal: fought at Shuanghekou and defeated the Ming general Li Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: then at Shuanghekou defeated Li Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 師還，進三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was advanced to third-class ashan i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was promoted to third-class ashan i hafan.

sentences.zh: 十八年八月，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Shunzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 洛多歡，舒裡渾弟。

translations.literal: Luoduhuan was Shulihun's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Luoduhuan was Shulihun's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 從軍，取旅順，圍錦州，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed the army, took Lüshun, and besieged Jinzhou, distinguishing himself in each.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he helped take Lüshun and besiege Jinzhou, earning merit in both.

sentences.zh: 崇德七年，從貝勒阿巴泰伐明，克順德府，先登，賜號「巴圖魯」。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongde he followed Beile Abatai against the Ming, captured Shunde Prefecture, was first over the wall, and was granted the title "Baturu."
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 7 he joined Beile Abatai's raid into Ming territory, was first into Shunde Prefecture, and received the title Baturu.

sentences.zh: 累進世職至一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: By successive promotions he rose in hereditary rank to first-class adaha hafan with the additional title tosoro hafan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to first-class adaha hafan with tosoro hafan.

sentences.zh: 崆古圖，亦舒裡渾弟也。

translations.literal: Kuanggutu was also Shulihun's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanggutu was another younger brother of Shulihun.

sentences.zh: 順治間，從靖南將軍陳泰徵福建，克興化府，先登。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi reign he followed General Jingnan Chen Tai in the campaign against Fujian, captured Xinghua Prefecture, and was first over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi he served under General Chen Tai in the Fujian campaign, took Xinghua Prefecture, and led the assault.

sentences.zh: 自巴牙喇壯達擢甲喇額真。

translations.literal: From bayara da he was promoted to jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from bayara da to jalan ejen.

sentences.zh: 十七年，洛多歡卒，襲世職。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Luoduhuan died, and he succeeded to the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoduhuan died in Shunzhi 17, he inherited the family rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，從副都統雅賚、阿喀尼等討耿進忠，自安慶向江西，敗賊小孤山，复彭澤、宜黃、崇仁、樂安諸縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he followed the vice commandants Yabai and Akeni and others in suppressing Geng Jingzhong, marched from Anqing toward Jiangxi, defeated the rebels at Xiaogushan, and recovered Pengze, Yihuang, Chongren, Le'an, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 he joined Vice Commandants Yabai and Akeni against Geng Jingzhong, advanced from Anqing into Jiangxi, routed the rebels at Xiaogushan, and retook Pengze, Yihuang, Chongren, Le'an, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 十五年，移師討吳三桂，攻萍鄉，敗其將夏國相，師下湖南。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the army shifted to suppress Wu Sangui, attacked Pingxiang, defeated his general Xia Guoxiang, and the force descended into Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 he turned against Wu Sangui, attacked Pingxiang, defeated Xia Guoxiang, and pushed the army into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，戰楓木嶺，敗其將吳國貴，复武岡。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he fought at Fengmuling, defeated Wu Sangui's general Wu Guogui, and recovered Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 he fought at Fengmuling, routed Wu Guogui, and retook Wugang.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 24.

sentences.zh: 子多博海，襲。

translations.literal: His son Duobohai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duobohai inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 特爾勒，舒裡渾孫也。

translations.literal: Te'erle was Shulihun's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Te'erle was Shulihun's grandson.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，從征南大將軍賚塔討吳世璠，敗其將何繼祖，奪石門坎、黃草壩；

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign he followed the southern expedition commander Laibao against Wu Shifan, defeated his general He Jizu, and seized Shimenkan and Huangcaba;
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he served under Laibao in the campaign against Wu Shifan, routed He Jizu, and took Shimenkan and Huangcaba;

sentences.zh: 乘夜拔嵩明、丹城，遂克雲南。

translations.literal: by night he stormed Songming and Dancheng and then captured Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: then by night seized Songming and Dancheng and helped take Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 又從都統希福逐馬寶，破胡國柱。

translations.literal: He also followed the commander Xifu in pursuing Ma Bao and defeated Hu Guozhu.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Commander Xifu in the pursuit of Ma Bao and the defeat of Hu Guozhu.

sentences.zh: 以功，予世職拜他勒布喇哈番。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the hereditary rank of baitalabura hafan.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he received the hereditary rank of baitalabura hafan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗為故勳臣雅巴海祈天：「乞轉生朕家！」

translations.literal: Taizu once prayed to Heaven on behalf of the former meritorious minister Yabahai: "Grant that he be reborn in my house!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once prayed Heaven on behalf of the old minister Yabahai: "Let him be reborn into my clan!"

sentences.zh: 又為布哈孫、朗格等八人祈曰：「宥其微失！」

translations.literal: He also prayed for Buhusun, Langge, and seven others, saying: "Pardon their minor faults!"
translations.idiomatic: He also prayed for Buhusun, Langge, and six others: "Forgive their small lapses!"

sentences.zh: 太祖未舉兵以前，有族難，侍者帕海死之，似即雅巴海。

translations.literal: Before Taizu raised arms, there was a clan feud; the attendant Pahai died in it—likely the same as Yabahai.
translations.idiomatic: Before Taizu took up arms there was a clan feud; his attendant Pahai died in it—probably Yabahai himself.

sentences.zh: 布哈孫等事不著。

translations.literal: The affairs of Buhusun and the others are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing further is recorded of Buhusun and the others.

sentences.zh: 巴篤理，世居佟佳，以地為氏。

translations.literal: Baduli's family had long resided at Tongjia and took the place as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Baduli's clan had long lived at Tongjia and took that place as their surname.

sentences.zh: 天命初，與其弟蒙阿圖來歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianming he came over with his younger brother Meng'atu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianming era he submitted with his younger brother Meng'atu.

sentences.zh: 太祖命編所屬為二牛錄，隸滿洲正白旗。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered their followers organized into two niru and enrolled under the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu organized their followers into two niru under the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 太祖察巴篤理才，使為扎爾固齊。

translations.literal: Taizu recognized Baduli's talent and made him a jarguci.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Baduli's ability, Taizu appointed him a jarguci.

sentences.zh: 積戰功，授游擊。

translations.literal: He accumulated battle merit and was granted the rank of guerrilla commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated service in the field he received the rank of guerrilla commandant.

sentences.zh: 十年，

translations.literal: In the tenth year,
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 10,

sentences.zh: 明發兵航海至旅順，繕完故城，駐軍以守。

translations.literal: the Ming sent troops by sea to Lüshun, repaired the old city, and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: the Ming sent troops by sea to Lüshun, rebuilt the old fort, and left a garrison.

sentences.zh: 巴篤理從貝勒莽爾古泰攻之，城下，盡殲明兵。

translations.literal: Baduli followed Beile Mang'ergutai in attacking it; the city fell and the Ming troops were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Baduli joined Beile Mang'ergutai's assault, took the city, and wiped out the Ming force.

sentences.zh: 十一年，明將毛文龍遣兵夜襲薩爾滸城，城兵砲矢交發，明兵退，結營。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Ming general Mao Wenlong sent troops to raid Sarihu City by night; the garrison answered with cannon and arrows, the Ming troops withdrew, and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 11 Mao Wenlong sent a night raid against Sarihu; the defenders met it with cannon and arrows, the Ming force fell back and made camp.

sentences.zh: 巴篤理率兵自山而下，大呼乘敵，敵潰走，追斬二百餘級。

translations.literal: Baduli led troops down from the mountain, shouting as he charged the enemy; the enemy broke and fled, and he pursued them, cutting down more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Baduli swept down from the hills with a shout, routed the enemy, and pursued them, taking more than two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從伐明，克遵化有功。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against the Ming and distinguished himself in the capture of Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 he joined the Ming campaign and distinguished himself at the capture of Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 太宗親酌金卮

translations.literal: The Emperor personally poured him a golden goblet
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally poured him wine from a golden cup

sentences.zh: 勞之，進二等參將。

translations.literal: to reward him and promoted him to second-class vice general.
translations.idiomatic: to honor him and promoted him to second-class vice general.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，從貝勒濟爾哈朗守永平。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he followed Beile Jirhalang in holding Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tiancong 4 he joined Beile Jirhalang in the defense of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 三月，明將張弘謨率兵來侵，甲喇額真圖魯什以四十人先，巴篤理與噶布什賢噶喇昂邦屯布祿以百人繼。

translations.literal: In the third month the Ming general Zhang Hongmo led troops to invade; Jalan Ejen Tulushi went ahead with forty men, and Baduli followed with Gabushixian Galang Angbang Tunbulu and a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhang Hongmo invaded; Tulushi led forty men as vanguard, and Baduli followed with Tunbulu and a hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 伏起，屯布祿敗走，巴篤理與圖魯什殿，力戰，其弟課約馬著矢且踣，巴篤理斬敵兵，奪馬授其弟，殪三十餘人，敵乃退。

translations.literal: Ambushers rose; Tunbulu was beaten and fled; Baduli and Tulushi held the rear and fought fiercely. Baduli's younger brother Keyue was struck by an arrow and nearly fell; Baduli cut down an enemy soldier, seized a horse and gave it to his brother, killed more than thirty men, and the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the ambush sprang, Tunbulu broke and ran; Baduli and Tulushi covered the retreat. Keyue was wounded and nearly unhorsed, so Baduli killed a foe, seized his mount for his brother, cut down thirty-odd men, and drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 五月，明兵圍灤州，貝勒阿敏守永平，不即赴援，城垂破，乃遣巴篤理率兵赴之，乘夜突圍入城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ming troops besieged Luanzhou; Beile Amin held Yongping and did not go promptly to the relief; as the city was on the verge of falling he sent Baduli with troops to its aid, and by night Baduli broke through the encirclement and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Luanzhou was besieged; Amin, holding Yongping, delayed relief until the city was near collapse, then sent Baduli, who broke through by night and entered the town.

sentences.zh: 方議並力堅守，敵發巨砲焚城樓，守將納穆泰等度力不能支，棄城依阿敏，阿敏亦棄永平東還。

translations.literal: Just as they were debating a united defense, the enemy fired great cannon and burned the gate tower; the garrison commanders Namutai and others judged they could not hold out, abandoned the city and joined Amin, and Amin too abandoned Yongping and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: As they debated a last stand, the enemy's heavy guns set the gate tower ablaze; Namutai and the other commanders saw the defense was hopeless, abandoned the city for Amin's camp, and Amin in turn abandoned Yongping and withdrew east.

sentences.zh: 廷議諸將罪，以巴篤理突圍赴援，釋勿論。

translations.literal: The court reviewed the generals' offenses; because Baduli had broken through to bring relief, he was excused.
translations.idiomatic: When the court reviewed the commanders' failures, Baduli was cleared because he had fought his way in to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 五年，授禮部承政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 5 he was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，使朝鮮，定職貢額數。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was sent to Korea to fix the quotas for tribute and offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 6 he was dispatched to Korea to set the tribute quotas.

sentences.zh: 八年八月，太宗自將伐明，巴篤理從，至應州，命與貝勒阿巴泰等取靈丘縣王家莊。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighth year the Emperor personally led a campaign against the Ming; Baduli followed him to Yingzhou and was ordered with Beile Abatai and others to take Wangjiazhuang in Lingqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tiancong 8 the Emperor led a campaign against the Ming; Baduli followed to Yingzhou and was ordered with Beile Abatai to take Wangjiazhuang in Lingqiu.

sentences.zh: 巴篤理督軍攻堡，既被創，猶奮擊，中流矢，卒。

translations.literal: Baduli directed the assault on a fort; though already wounded, he still fought hard, was struck by a stray arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Baduli led the assault on a fort; though wounded he kept fighting until a stray arrow killed him.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之泣下，曰：「此朕舊臣，轉戰數十年，歿於

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard it he wept and said: "This is an old servant of mine who fought for decades and died on
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept when he heard and said: "He was an old servant of mine who fought for decades and fell on

sentences.zh: 疆場，深可惜也！」

translations.literal: the battlefield—it is deeply to be regretted!"
translations.idiomatic: the battlefield—this is a grievous loss!"

sentences.zh: 卹贈三等副將。

translations.literal: Posthumous gifts were conferred and he was granted third-class vice general.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the rank of third-class vice general.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，追諡敏壯。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously given the temple name Minzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 he was posthumously given the posthumous name Minzhuang.

sentences.zh: 子卓羅，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Zhuoluo has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuoluo has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 蒙阿圖，自牛錄額真累擢梅勒額真，坐私立屯莊，罷。

translations.literal: Meng'atu rose from niru ejen by successive promotions to meiren ejen, but was dismissed for privately establishing estate farms.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'atu rose from niru ejen to meiren ejen, but was dismissed for establishing private estates.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從伐明，敗敵於遵化。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against the Ming and defeated the enemy at Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 he joined the Ming campaign and routed the enemy at Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 逾年師還，上自出郊宴勞。

translations.literal: The next year, when the army returned, the Emperor himself went out beyond the suburbs to feast and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned the following year, the Emperor went out to the suburbs to feast and reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 授游擊世職，擢工部承政，

translations.literal: He was granted a hereditary guerrilla commandant's rank and promoted to Minister of Works,
translations.idiomatic: He received a hereditary guerrilla rank and was made Minister of Works,

sentences.zh: 同知事。

translations.literal: with concurrent charge of the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: with concurrent charge of the ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋命帥師伐瓦爾喀，俘其人。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to lead troops against the Warka and took captives.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to lead a campaign against the Warka and took prisoners.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，以老解職，召見，諭之曰：「爾等舊臣，朕見之輒心喜，可不時來見也！」

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he was relieved of office on account of age; summoned to audience, he was instructed: "You are old ministers; whenever I see you my heart rejoices—you may come to see me from time to time!"
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 he retired on account of age; when summoned he was told: "You old ministers always gladden me when I see you—come visit whenever you wish!"

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 國初諸將，事太祖創業复佐太宗從征伐而戰死者，勞薩、圖魯什功最高，巴篤理、穆克譚、納爾特與相亞，達珠瑚為俘所賊。

translations.literal: Among the founding generals who served Taizu in establishing the enterprise and then aided Taizong on campaigns until they died in battle, Laosa and Tulushi rank highest in merit; Baduli, Muketan, and Na'erte stand next to them; Dazhuhu was killed by captives.
translations.idiomatic: Of the early generals who built the dynasty under Taizu and then died campaigning under Taizong, Laosa and Tulushi stand highest; Baduli, Muketan, and Na'erte rank next; Dazhuhu was killed by prisoners.

sentences.zh: 順治中，皆追諡。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi reign posthumous names were conferred on them all.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi they all received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 納爾特事具其父雅希禪傳中。

translations.literal: Na'erte's career is given in full in the biography of his father Yaxichan.
translations.idiomatic: Na'erte's career is recorded in his father Yaxichan's biography.

sentences.zh: 來歸，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: He submitted and was appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He came over and was made niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 從太祖征伐。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu on campaign.

sentences.zh: 穆克譚，戴佳氏，世居杭澗，隸哈達。

translations.literal: Muketan, of the Daijia clan, had long resided at Hangjian and was subject to Hada.
translations.idiomatic: Muketan, of the Daijia clan, came from Hangjian in Hada territory.

sentences.zh: 穆克譚從其父兄率眾征伐，戰必陷陣，攻則先登，賜號「巴圖魯」。

translations.literal: Muketan followed his father and elder brother leading troops on campaigns; in battle he always broke into the enemy ranks, and in assaults he was first over the wall; he was granted the title "Baturu."
translations.idiomatic: Following his father and elder brother into war, he always led the charge and was first over the wall; he received the title Baturu.

sentences.zh: 有查海胡色者，叛太祖歸哈達，穆克譚從其父兄追之，戰，其父兄皆死。

translations.literal: There was one Chahai Huse who rebelled against Taizu and went over to Hada; Muketan followed his father and elder brother in pursuit; in the fight both his father and elder brother died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chahai Huse rebelled and fled to Hada, Muketan followed his father and brother in pursuit; both were killed in the fight.

sentences.zh: 從子厄爾諾亦叛歸哈達，穆克譚單騎逐斬之。

translations.literal: His nephew E'ernuo also rebelled and went over to Hada; Muketan pursued alone on horseback and cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: When his nephew E'ernuo also defected to Hada, Muketan rode after him alone and killed him.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were organized he was placed in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命元年，從伐瓦爾喀，戰敗，諸將孟庫噶哈皆走，舒賽、阿爾虎達將為敵得，穆克譚與燕布里等八人衝敵陣，援之出。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianming he followed a campaign against the Warka; the army was defeated and the generals Mengku Gaha all fled; Shusai and Arhuda were about to be taken by the enemy when Muketan with Yanburi and seven others charged the enemy line and rescued them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 1, campaigning against the Warka, the army was beaten and Mengku Gaha's officers fled; Muketan and seven others including Yanburi broke into the enemy line and rescued Shusai and Arhuda as they were about to be captured.

sentences.zh: 師還，太祖譴孟庫噶哈，奪所獲畀穆克譚。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Taizu rebuked Mengku Gaha and took what he had captured and gave it to Muketan.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Taizu rebuked Mengku Gaha and transferred his spoils to Muketan.

sentences.zh: 六年，叛去，我師追之，戰不利。

translations.literal: In the sixth year someone rebelled and fled; our army pursued but the battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 6 a defector fled and the pursuit went badly.

sentences.zh: 穆克譚從伐明，攻耀州，先登，克之，命戍焉。

translations.literal: Muketan followed a campaign against the Ming, attacked Yaozhou, was first over the wall, captured it, and was ordered to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Muketan joined a Ming campaign, was first into Yaozhou, took the city, and was left to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 蒙古人海色與其黨策馬大呼，直前刺殺海色，餘悉潰。

translations.literal: The Mongol Haise and his followers spurred their horses forward with a great shout; Muketan charged straight ahead and killed Haise, and the rest all fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mongol Haise and his band charged shouting, Muketan rode straight at them, killed Haise, and routed the rest.

sentences.zh: 以功授二等副將。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted second-class vice general.
translations.idiomatic: For this he received the rank of second-class vice general.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，各旗設調遣大臣，以穆克譚佐本旗。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, each banner was given a dispatch minister, and Muketan assisted his own banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne each banner received a dispatch minister; Muketan served in that role for his banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年四月，從伐朝鮮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tiancong 1 he joined the Korean campaign.

sentences.zh: 六月，阿山、阿達海兄弟叛，將歸明，貝勒阿敏夜帥師追之，穆克譚從，射阿達海，阿達海力戰，抽刀斫穆克譚墜馬，幾殆，卒挾以俱還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the brothers Ashan and Adahai rebelled and were about to go over to the Ming; Beile Amin led troops in pursuit by night; Muketan followed, shot Adahai; Adahai fought hard, drew his sword and struck Muketan from his horse, nearly killing him, but in the end they seized both brothers and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Ashan and Adahai rebelled and fled toward the Ming; Amin pursued by night with Muketan, who shot Adahai; Adahai fought back, knocked Muketan from his horse with his blade and nearly killed him, but both brothers were seized and brought back.

sentences.zh: 五年，從伐明，圍大凌河，穆克譚以本旗兵從固山額真宗室篇古當城西南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed a campaign against the Ming and besieged Dalinghe; Muketan with his banner's troops followed Gushan Ejen the clansman Panggu in holding the southwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 5 he joined the siege of Dalinghe; Muketan commanded his banner's troops under Gushan Ejen Panggu on the city's southwest.

sentences.zh: 城兵出挑戰，圖賴先進，穆克譚從之，薄壕，舍騎步戰，將迫敵入壕。

translations.literal: The garrison came out to challenge; Tulei advanced first and Muketan followed; they pressed close to the moat, dismounted to fight on foot, and were about to drive the enemy into the ditch.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison sallied forth, Tulei led and Muketan followed; they reached the moat, fought on foot, and were pressing the enemy back into the ditch.

sentences.zh: 城上矢

translations.literal: Arrows from the wall
translations.idiomatic: Arrows from the wall

sentences.zh: 矢競發，城兵續出，奮拒力戰，歿於陣。

translations.literal: flew in volleys; more garrison troops came out, fought fiercely in resistance, and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: rained down; fresh defenders poured out, fought hard, and he fell in the field.

sentences.zh: 太宗惜之，曰：「穆克譚我舊臣，不值於此畢命也！」

translations.literal: Taizong grieved and said: "Muketan was an old servant of mine—it was not fitting that he should end his life here!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him, saying: "Muketan was an old servant of mine—he ought not to have died like this!"

sentences.zh: 贈一等副將，世襲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted first-class vice general with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made first-class vice general, inheritable by his heirs.

sentences.zh: 順治間，追諡忠勇，立碑墓道。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi reign he was posthumously given the name Zhongyong and a stele was erected on the road to his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi he received the posthumous name Zhongyong and a stele was raised at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 子愛音塔穆。

translations.literal: His son was Aiyintamu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Aiyintamu.

sentences.zh: 愛音塔穆襲父爵，兼領穆克譚舊轄牛錄，益壯丁五十。

translations.literal: Aiyintamu succeeded to his father's rank, also took charge of Muketan's former niru, and was given fifty additional able-bodied men.
translations.idiomatic: Aiyintamu inherited his father's rank, took over Muketan's old niru, and received fifty additional fighting men.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關破李自成。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes and defeated Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he crossed into China and helped defeat Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 旋從豫親王多鐸徇河南，與梅勒額真沙爾瑚達屢敗賊，逐賊至潼關，為殿，賊自後來襲，三至三卻，愛音塔穆功也。

translations.literal: He then followed Prince Yu Dodo in a sweep of Henan; with Meiren Ejen Sharhuda he repeatedly defeated the rebels, pursued them to Tongguan, and served as rearguard; when the rebels attacked from behind three times he drove them back three times—this was Aiyintamu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Prince Dodo's sweep of Henan; with Meiren Ejen Sharhuda he repeatedly routed the rebels, pursued them to Tongguan, and as rearguard beat back three successive attacks from the rear—Aiyintamu's work.

sentences.zh: 二年，河南既平，從定江南。

translations.literal: In the second year, once Henan was pacified, he followed in the pacification of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2, after Henan was pacified, he joined the conquest of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗下湖廣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang south into Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Shunzhi 6 he followed Prince Jirhalang into Huguang.

sentences.zh: 時明桂王由榔駐武岡，湖南諸郡縣半為明守。

translations.literal: At that time the Ming Prince of Gui Youlang was stationed at Wugang, and half the prefectures and counties of Hunan were still held by the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui, Youlang, held Wugang, and half of Hunan's prefectures and counties remained in Ming hands.

sentences.zh: 愛音塔穆帥師自長沙而南，克寶慶，擊馬進忠、王進才皆有功。

translations.literal: Aiyintamu led troops south from Changsha, captured Baqing, and distinguished himself in fighting Ma Jinzhong and Wang Jincai.
translations.idiomatic: Aiyintamu marched south from Changsha, took Baqing, and distinguished himself against Ma Jinzhong and Wang Jincai.

sentences.zh: 自成將劉體純與其黨袁宗第等屯洪江為十寨，緣沅江拒守。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng's general Liu Tichun with his partisans Yuan Zongdi and others encamped at Hongjiang in ten stockades, holding the line along the Yuan River.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's general Liu Tichun and Yuan Zongdi's band held ten stockades at Hongjiang along the Yuan River.

sentences.zh: 愛音塔穆與尚書阿哈尼堪督軍渡江，連破賊寨，賊潰，遂與阿哈尼堪駐守沅州。

translations.literal: Aiyintamu with Minister Ahanikan directed the army across the river, broke the rebel stockades in succession, the rebels fled, and he then garrisoned Yuanzhou with Ahanikan.
translations.idiomatic: Aiyintamu and Minister Ahanikan crossed the river, stormed the rebel camps one after another, routed the enemy, and garrisoned Yuanzhou together.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊將王強來犯，與阿哈尼堪共擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the rebel general Wang Qiang came to attack; together with Ahanikan he drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, when the rebel general Wang Qiang attacked, he and Ahanikan joined forces and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 九年，遇恩詔，累進二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, benefiting from an amnesty edict, he was advanced in succession to second-rank jingkini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 an amnesty edict raised his rank step by step to second-class jingkini hafan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，從靖南將軍珠瑪喇四萬，列象？

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he followed Pacification-of-the-South General Zhuma'la, leading forty thousand troops and deploying an elephant formation,
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he marched under Pacification-of-the-South General Zhuma'la with forty thousand men, drawing up an elephant formation,

sentences.zh: ，據山峪，方相？

translations.literal: holding the mountain passes as the two sides faced each other in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: seized the mountain passes, and the armies settled into a standoff.

sentences.zh: 略廣東，時明將李定國攻新會，平南王尚可喜赴援，定國有持。

translations.literal: skirmishing in Guangdong. At that time the Ming general Li Dingguo was attacking Xinhui; Prince Pingnan Shang Kexi went to reinforce, and Dingguo held his ground.
translations.idiomatic: then pushed into Guangdong. While the Ming general Li Dingguo besieged Xinhui, Prince Pingnan Shang Kexi hurried to relieve the city, and the two sides remained deadlocked.

sentences.zh: 愛音塔穆等師至，合擊大破之，逐北二十餘裡，定國遁去。

translations.literal: When Aiyintamu's army and the others arrived, they joined in a combined attack and inflicted a great defeat, pursuing north for more than twenty li; Dingguo fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Aiyintamu's column arrived, the combined force routed the enemy, chased them more than twenty li, and Li Dingguo fled.

sentences.zh: 十二年閏五月，論功，進一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the twelfth year, his merit was assessed and he was advanced to first-rank jingkini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of Shunzhi 12 his service was rewarded with promotion to first-class jingkini hafan.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 19.

sentences.zh: 子公圖，襲。

translations.literal: His son Gongtu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongtu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從撫遠大將軍費揚古徵噶爾丹昭莫多，戰勝，進三等伯。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he followed Pacification-of-the-Distance Grand General Feiyanggu in campaigning against Galdan at Jao Modo, was victorious in battle, and was advanced to third-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 he joined Grand General Feiyanggu's campaign against Galdan at Jao Modo, won the battle, and was raised to third-class baron.

sentences.zh: 子永泰，降襲二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: His son Yongtai inherited at a reduced rank as second-rank jingkini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongtai succeeded at a reduced rank to second-class jingkini hafan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，改一等子，世襲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the title was changed to first-class viscount with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the hereditary title was revised to first-class viscount.

sentences.zh: =達珠瑚=達珠瑚，兆佳氏，先世居訥殷。

translations.literal: =Dazhuhu= Dazhuhu, of the Zhaojia clan, had ancestors who long resided at Neyin.
translations.idiomatic: =Dazhuhu= Dazhuhu, of the Zhaojia clan, came from Neyin.

sentences.zh: 祖達爾楚，國初來歸。

translations.literal: His grandfather Da'erchu came over at the beginning of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Da'erchu submitted in the dynasty's earliest days.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲正藍旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were established he was enrolled in the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were organized he was assigned to the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 達珠瑚初任牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Dazhuhu was first appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhuhu began as niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 從太祖伐烏喇，斬級四千。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu in campaigning against Ula and beheaded four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Nurhaci against Ula and took four thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 從克西林屯，俘其人以歸；

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Xilintun and brought back its people as captives;
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Xilintun and returned with prisoners;

sentences.zh: 追者至，還擊敗之，斬級五千。

translations.literal: when pursuers arrived he turned back, defeated them, and beheaded five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: when pursuers caught up he wheeled about, routed them, and took five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 從伐葉赫，斬級三百，俘五十人。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Yehe, beheaded three hundred, and took fifty captives.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Yehe he killed three hundred and captured fifty.

sentences.zh: 遇明人越境採參，斬三十人，俘六人。

translations.literal: He encountered Ming men crossing the border to gather ginseng, beheaded thirty, and took six captives.
translations.idiomatic: He came upon Ming subjects gathering ginseng across the border, killed thirty, and took six prisoners.

sentences.zh: 敵侵寧古塔，出戰，斬其將及兵百，獲甲百副、馬三百匹。

translations.literal: When the enemy invaded Ningguta he went out to fight, beheaded their general and a hundred soldiers, and captured a hundred suits of armor and three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When enemies raided Ningguta he marched out, killed their general and a hundred men, and seized a hundred suits of armor and three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 授三等副將。

translations.literal: He was appointed third-class vice general.
translations.idiomatic: He was made third-class vice general.

sentences.zh: 天命十一年，伐東海瓦爾喀部，又伐卦爾察部，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianming he campaigned against the Eastern Sea Walgari tribe and again against the Guarca tribe; in both he distinguished himself.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 11 he fought the Eastern Sea Walgari and then the Guarca tribes, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，設十六大臣，伊遜及達珠瑚佐鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, sixteen great ministers were appointed; Yisun and Dazhuhu assisted the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji took the throne he created sixteen great ministers; Yisun and Dazhuhu served as deputies of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，太宗伐朝鮮，克義州，留兵駐守，命達珠瑚分將之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong Taizong campaigned against Korea, took Uiju, left troops to garrison it, and ordered Dazhuhu to command a division.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 Hong Taiji invaded Korea, captured Uiju, left a garrison, and put Dazhuhu in command of part of the force.

sentences.zh: 旋复帥師伐瓦爾喀。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again led troops to campaign against Walgari.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led another expedition against Walgari.

sentences.zh: 師還，為俘卒所賊。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was killed by captive soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he was killed by prisoners.

sentences.zh: 八年，以其子翁阿岱襲三等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his son Wengadai inherited third-rank meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 his son Wengadai succeeded to third-rank meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 太宗復遣將伐瓦爾喀，因誡之曰：「前遣達珠瑚，以？

translations.literal: Taizong again sent generals to campaign against Walgari and admonished them, saying: "The last time I sent Dazhuhu, because he was not cautious
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji sent another force against Walgari he warned them: "When I dispatched Dazhuhu before, his lack of caution

sentences.zh: 見害。

translations.literal: he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: got him killed.

sentences.zh: 念其從事久，有勞，方令襲世職。

translations.literal: Remembering his long service and his labors, I only then allowed his hereditary office to be inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering his long service, I allowed his son to inherit the title only because of that.

sentences.zh: 汝曹未能如達珠瑚之功，儻不自慎，欲覬例外恩，不可得也。」

translations.literal: You cannot match Dazhuhu's achievements; if you are not careful yourselves and hope for exceptional favor, you will not obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: You have not earned what Dazhuhu earned. If you fail to watch yourselves and expect special favor, you will not receive it."

sentences.zh: 順治間，追諡襄敏。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi reign he was posthumously given the name Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi he received the posthumous name Xiangmin, "Assisting and Keen."

sentences.zh: 翁阿岱襲職為甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Wengadai inherited office as jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Wengadai inherited the rank of jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 從伐虎爾哈，加半個前程。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Hurha and was given half a step of seniority.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Hurha and received half a step of seniority.

sentences.zh: 累遷都察院參政、正藍旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to censorate commissioner and meiren ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the censorate to become meiren ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 時方攻錦州急，命與梅勒額真多積禮帥師屯戍，譏逋逃。

translations.literal: At that time the assault on Jinzhou was pressing; he was ordered with Meiren Ejen Duojili to lead troops in garrison duty and apprehend deserters.
translations.idiomatic: While the siege of Jinzhou was at its height, he and Meiren Ejen Duojili were ordered to garrison the lines and hunt down deserters.

sentences.zh: 崇德六年，從圍錦州，與明總督洪承疇戰，屢勝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongde he followed in the siege of Jinzhou and fought Ming Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, winning repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 6 he joined the siege of Jinzhou and repeatedly defeated the Ming governor-general Hong Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 尋進攻松山，力戰，沒於陣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he advanced to attack Songshan, fought fiercely, and died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: He then pushed on to Songshan, fought hard, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 賚白金千兩，進一等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: He was granted a thousand taels of white silver and advanced to first-rank meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted a thousand taels of silver and posthumously raised him to first-rank meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 無子，以弟之子濟木布襲。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brother's son Jimubu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his nephew Jimubu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，降襲一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign the inherited title was reduced to first-rank ashan-i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi the hereditary title descended at a reduced rank to first-class ashan-i hafan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，改一等男，世襲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong it was changed to first-class baron with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the title was revised to first-class baron, inheritable in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：國之將興，必有熊羆之士，不二心之臣，致身事主，蹈死不反顧，乃能拓土破敵，弼成大業。

translations.literal: =Commentary= The commentary says: When a state is about to rise, there must be bear-and-tiger warriors and ministers of undivided heart who devote their persons to serving their lord, tread death without turning back—only then can territory be expanded, enemies broken, and the great enterprise assisted to completion.
translations.idiomatic: =Commentary= The historians write: A rising state needs warriors fierce as bears and tigers and ministers whose loyalty never wavers—men who give their bodies to their lord and meet death without a backward glance. Only then can borders widen, enemies fall, and the great work be brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 揚古利負大將才略，功視額亦都、費英東伯仲間；

translations.literal: Yangguli possessed the talent and strategy of a great general; his achievements rank between Eidu and Fei Yingdong;
translations.idiomatic: Yangguli had the talent of a field marshal; his achievements stand alongside those of Eidu and Fei Yingdong;

sentences.zh: 勞薩、圖魯什驍勇冠軍，戰必將選鋒陷陣；

translations.literal: Laosa and Tulushi were foremost in fierce courage; in battle they always led the chosen vanguard in breaking the enemy ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Laosa and Tulushi were the bravest men in the army, always leading the vanguard into the enemy line;

sentences.zh: 若拜山三世？

translations.literal: Jueluo Baishan's three generations gave their lives in loyal service;
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Baishan's line gave three generations of steadfast loyalty;

sentences.zh: 忠，西喇布、達音布、巴篤理等以死勤事，亦其亞也。

translations.literal: Xilabu, Dayinbu, Baduli, and others who died in diligent service to the ruler also rank next to them.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal service: Xilabu, Dayinbu, Baduli, and others who died in the ruler's service rank just below.

sentences.zh: 觀太祖祈天之語，惓惓於舊將；

translations.literal: Observing Taizu's words in praying to Heaven, he was earnest toward his old generals;
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu's prayers to Heaven one sees how tenderly he remembered his old commanders;

sentences.zh: 太宗以達珠瑚為戒，又以恭袞不從令，雖陣亡，猶付吏議。

translations.literal: Taizong took Dazhuhu as a warning, and because Gonggun did not obey orders, even though he died on the field he was still referred to the officials for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji held Dazhuhu up as a warning, and when Gonggun disobeyed orders—even though he died in battle—the case still went before the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 其申軍律，惜將材，恩威兼盡，開國基於是矣。

translations.literal: In enforcing military law, cherishing the talent of generals, and combining kindness with authority to the full, the foundation of the founding of the state was laid thereby.
translations.idiomatic: In enforcing discipline, cherishing able commanders, and wielding kindness and severity together, the dynasty laid the foundation of its rise.
